LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. The New England Patriots and Drake Maye are riding a three-game winning streak into their primetime matchup with the Chicago Bears and former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams on Thursday Night Football. Williams is making his second straight start after he missed three games earlier this season with a hamstring injury. The star quarterback showed no signs of rust in Week 6, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, improving the Bears to 4-2 this season. Chicago is favored in this matchup, and it needs every win it can get with the NFC North sporting four teams over .500 through the first six weeks. The Bears may be getting a little extra love in this matchup because of all the injuries for the Patriots, who have been decimated at receiver (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on IR) and on their offensive line. Still, New England has won three games in a row, and Maye is back in the MVP conversation with 10 touchdown passes during that streak. He has a tough matchup ahead against a Chicago team that is in the top 10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense this season. So, how should bettors attack Thursday’s showdown? In the leadup to this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made a bunch of game picks, prop bet selections and more. I’ve decided to share some of our favorites all in one place to help bettors get the most of this primetime matchup between two playoff contenders in Week 7. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Patriots vs. Bears Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook New England Patriots vs. Chicago Bears UNDER 50.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan Drake Maye OVER 1.5 Passing Touchdowns (-116) – Peter Dewey Colston Loveland Anytime TD (+170) – Peter Dewey D’Andre Swift UNDER 61.5 Rushing Yards (-115) – Peter Dewey This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for this matchup in his Road to 272 column , where he picks every game of the NFL season. He’s taking the UNDER even with two star quarterbacks facing off: Unless I'm missing something, I'm not quite sure why the total for this game is in the 50s. Sure, the Bears' offense is much more explosive with Caleb Williams at quarterback, but even with that being the case, these two offenses rank 12th and 14th in EPA per play this season and seventh and 12th in success rate. A high total would make sense if the two defenses in this game were bad, but they rank in the top half of the league in most metrics. In fact, the Bears' defense comes into this game ranking fourth in opponent success rate. The Patriots' offense is also dealing with some injuries. A.J. Brown is questionable, and Romeo Doubs is on IR. Their run game can't be relied on to help out the injuries at wide receiver, as it's been largely ineffective all season. I'll bet the UNDER on Thursday Night Football for the second straight week. Maye started the season in an awful slump, throwing just one score and six picks in his first three games. Since then, he’s flipped the script, tossing 10 scores (at least three in each game) over the last three weeks, leading New England to wins over Buffalo, Las Vegas and the New York Jets. Maye is right back in the mix to win the MVP, and I like this matchup against a Chicago defense that has allowed nine passing scores in 2026 and was torched by Bryce Young and Jordan Love already this season. The Bears have benefitted from some soft scheduling in terms of the quarterbacks they’ve faced, but Love threw for 367 yards against them in Week 5, and Chicago has allowed the 15th-most passing yards in the league. New England loves to throw the ball, and I think the odds for this prop are pretty favorable considering the fact that Maye threw 31 touchdown passes in 2025. Bears tight end Colston Loveland had a breakout showing in Week 6, catching six of his seven targets for 65 yards and a score. Williams only threw one touchdown in Week 6, but Loveland was targeted multiple times in the end zone – Caleb just missed him for a second score. Last season, the young tight end really came on in the second half, finishing the campaign with six touchdown receptions. He’s only picked up one in 2026, and New England has allowed just one receiving score to the position this season. Still, Loveland’s role is growing with 21 targets over the last three games. He’s a solid bet at this price after his best game of the season. D’Andre Swift has a ton of carries for the Bears this season, handling 94 touches for 398 yards and six scores on the ground, but he hasn’t been super efficient since Week 1. Swift ran for 124 yards on 18 carries against Carolina in the season opener, yet he has just one other game (Week 3 against Philadelphia) where he’s picked up over 60 rushing yards. Backup Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has been banged up, but Swift still split time with Roschon Johnson in Week 6 and has played just 56.7 percent of the Bears’ snaps this season. New England is allowing just 3.9 yards per carry in the 2026 campaign, and I wouldn’t be shocked if Swift came up short of this rushing total again on Thursday. He has averaged less than four yards per carry in two of the last three weeks, putting up 58, 43 and 44 rushing yards during that stretch. Even if the volume is there for the veteran back, I think he’s a fade candidate in Week 7. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. away.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The return of Chicago's standout defender alongside franchise quarterback Caleb Williams has helped put the Bears back on track, as they are the winners of two straight after starting the season just 3-2, including a pair of divisional losses to the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers. After missing the first five games of the season, Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon already appears to be in midseason form. Just a week removed from tying the NFL record for sacks in a single game by a cornerback, the 2022 second-round pick produced another strong outing in Chicago's 30-24 Thursday night win over the New England Patriots. Gordon, who missed the entirety of training camp due to a calf injury, has struggled to stay on the field over the last two years. In April 2025, the star defensive back became the highest-paid slot corner in the NFL, signing a three-year, $40 million deal to stay in the Windy City. Since the payday, the former Husky has played in just seven games, missing most of last season with soft tissue injuries. In just five days, the former second-round pick has erased any doubts about living up to his new contract, recording 9 tackles, 5 for loss, and 4 sacks in his first two games back. On Thursday night, Gordon picked up right where he left off in his season debut against the Atlanta Falcons, posting 5 tackles, 2 for loss, and a sack in the primetime victory over New England. Despite missing the first month of the season, the defensive back is tied for the most sacks on the Bears with defensive end Austin Booker. Winning their first of three consecutive primetime games, Chicago will head west next week to take on the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football before hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers the following Sunday night. With the core of their secondary now back and seemingly better than ever, the Bears defense is ready to hold up their end of the bargain as they look to contend for an NFC title. home.headline: Report: Bears tight end Cole Kmet's injury is likely season-ending
home.blurb: When Cole Kmet immediately grabbed his knee after being tackled in last night’s game, I hoped he’d just taken an awkward hit and would walk it off, just as we’ve seen so often during his seven-year Chicago Bears career. Then the cart came out for him, and I hoped it would just be precautionary. I reached out to a source to corroborate Rapoport’s report and was told it’s believed to be a torn ACL. UPDATED: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed that Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season and will be placed on injured reserve. “I’ve got so much respect for the player that he is, but also the person, the leader,” Johnson said about Kmet via the Score’s Chris Emma. “He’s everything we want to be about here. He’s one of the glue guys. He’s one of the guys that I can count on, whether it’s a messaging standpoint or getting the pulse of the team. He’s going to be sorely missed. Really, he’s Chicago. He’s been here his whole life, and he’s a big part of our heartbeat. So, it stinks, it does, I hate it for him, I hate it for his teammates as well.” But then head coach Ben Johnson met the media after the game and didn’t seem optimistic, saying it didn’t look very good. The Bears have yet to make an official statement, but according to Ian Rapoport , the NFL Insider for ESPN and NFL Network, Kmet is “believed to have suffered a serious, likely season-ending knee injury.” He added that Kmet will undergo more tests this morning and “until those results come back, there is no finality.” “I don’t have the words to describe what Cole is to me, what Cole is to this team, to this organization,” Caleb Williams said about Kmet in his postgame press conference. “He’s the longest-tenured Bear, I believe. He’s been through it. So, it’s challenging; it’s tough. I’ll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. Cole has been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, the second year, and now through this year. So, I can only do the same for him.” Kmet, drafted with the 43rd overall pick in the 2020 draft, is the longest-tenured Bear, and having grown up in suburban Lake Barrington, Illinois, as a Bears fan, he’s had Navy and Orange in his blood his whole life. Last month, Kmet wrote an article for The Player’s Tribune about his lifelong love of the Bears. I just want to win games and represent for this city, and for this team that I’ve loved since way back when I got that badass Urlacher jersey for Christmas. I want to do all I can to help bring another Lombardi Trophy home to Chicago. And hopefully we can all join together to make that happen this season, because I’d love to see all of you on Michigan Avenue for a big parade this winter if everything goes our way. Kmet did a lot of the little things on the football field to help the Bears win games, so his contributions will definitely be missed, but what he brings to the locker room as a team leader will be missed as well.

All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (+3.5) Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons (+3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans (+1.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16 Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset. Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18 Miami Dolphins (+4.5) at New York Jets The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 Cincinnati Bengals (+3) at Baltimore Ravens The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset. Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23 New York Giants (+10) at Houston Texans Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory. Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23 Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close. Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21 Green Bay Packers (+3) at Detroit Lions Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33 Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders (+4.5) This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. Pick: Rams 28, Raiders 27 Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) at Seattle Seahawks Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close. Their other victories have come against the Falcons and Cincinnati. In both the Cinci and Tampa games, the Steelers featured late-game heroics to claim victory, using the wiles of 42-year old quarterback Aaron Rodger s and the leg of kicker Chris Boswell , who had hit 4-field goals from over 50-yards out. Rodgers has just under 15-hundred yards passing and a dozen touchdowns on the year. His leading receiver is DK Metcalf with 318-yards. Jaylen Warren leads the team in rushing with 460-yards. With both teams coming off big wins in Week 6, let's take a look at the matchup and the bold predictions for Week 7 in Paris, France. Chris Boswell kicks five field goals, two from 50-plus © Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Boswell is 13-for-17 on field goals this season, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints' receiving group could be even more dangerous. away.headline: Steelers' TJ Watt pops up on injury report with new concern
away.blurb: The former Defensive Player of the Year didn’t practice on Wednesday for a rest designation. But, then he was limited in practice on Thursday because of a calf injury. This is a new injury to the public. There was some good defensive news coming out of the Steelers’ injury report, though. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday after not practicing the day prior with a wrist injury, so that was improvement. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was also limited with a groin issue, the same designation as Wednesday. Related Articles Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Pittsburgh Steelers haven’t been able to catch a break from injuries the last few weeks. It seems like a new star player is being added to the injury report each week. Thursday’s injury report included a surprising name, one that Steelers fans wish wasn’t on the list: edge rusher T.J. Watt. It’s unclear when or how Watt suffered the calf injury. But, now there’s a possibility, even if just a slight one, that Watt could miss Sunday’s game in Paris against the New Orleans Saints . Watt being absent for a game is always a loss for the Steelers. He can always make big and important plays for his team. Through six games this season, Watt’s recorded 4.5 sacks (tied for eighth in the league), 15 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. Veteran tackle Cameron Heyward didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday for rest designations, but he should be good to go come Sunday. Safety DeShon Elliott recorded his second-straight full practice on Thursday, meaning he’ll likely play on Sunday. It would mark Elliott’s first game since last October after he suffered an MCL sprain, hyperextended knee and a hamstring injury. Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. "Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar," Knox wrote. "Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles." Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline.

away.blurb: Saints Final Injury Report: Ruiz, Shepherd questionable for Steelers game in Paris – Crescent City Sports menu The New Orleans Saints will take a healthier roster into Sunday’s international matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, but questions remain about two key veterans as the teams prepare for their Week 7 showdown at Stade de France. Right guard Cesar Ruiz and defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd were listed as questionable on the Saints’ final injury report Friday. Both players are dealing with issues that could affect New Orleans on both sides of the line of scrimmage in its meeting with Pittsburgh. Ruiz, who sustained a knee injury during last Sunday’s 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, returned to practice Friday on a limited basis after missing the first two sessions of the week. His status will be worth watching, with rookie Jeremiah Wright a potential replacement if Ruiz cannot play. Shepherd was a late-week concern after missing Friday’s practice with an illness. He had participated fully Wednesday and Thursday but remains questionable. Shepherd has missed the Saints’ last two games while dealing with the illness. The Saints received encouraging news at linebacker, where Kaden Elliss and Anfernee Jennings both practiced fully Friday. Elliss has been working his way back from a calf injury, while Jennings has been dealing with a knee injury. Both are expected to be available against Pittsburgh. Kicker Daniel Carlson also returned to practice after missing the first two sessions for personal reasons. As he and his wife are still expecting the birth of their fourth child, Carlson traveled to France to rejoin the team and was a full participant Friday. With potentially challenging weather conditions including the chance for some rain and cross winds expected for the game, New Orleans will be glad to have the veteran specialist in tow Sunday. Running back Alvin Kamara remained limited with a back injury but was not assigned a game-status designation. Quarterback Tyler Shough, who has been managing a left-hand injury, practiced fully throughout the week. Other Saints listed as full participants Friday included running back C.J. Donaldson, cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry, quarterback Spencer Rattler, defensive lineman Davon Godchaux and offensive lineman Asim Richards, who was added to the report with a hand injury. Pittsburgh will be without wide receiver Ben Skowronek and cornerback Brandin Echols, both ruled out after missing practice throughout the week with calf and hamstring injuries, respectively. Running back Rico Dowdle and safety DeShon Elliott were listed as questionable. Dowdle was limited throughout the week with a knee injury after returning to action last Sunday, while Elliott participated fully in the first two sessions and was listed as a full participant for Friday’s estimated report. home.headline: Saints Final Injury Report: Ruiz, Shepherd questionable for Steelers in Paris
home.blurb: Saints Final Injury Report: Ruiz, Shepherd questionable for Steelers game in Paris – Crescent City Sports menu The New Orleans Saints will take a healthier roster into Sunday’s international matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, but questions remain about two key veterans as the teams prepare for their Week 7 showdown at Stade de France. Right guard Cesar Ruiz and defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd were listed as questionable on the Saints’ final injury report Friday. Both players are dealing with issues that could affect New Orleans on both sides of the line of scrimmage in its meeting with Pittsburgh. Ruiz, who sustained a knee injury during last Sunday’s 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, returned to practice Friday on a limited basis after missing the first two sessions of the week. His status will be worth watching, with rookie Jeremiah Wright a potential replacement if Ruiz cannot play. Shepherd was a late-week concern after missing Friday’s practice with an illness. He had participated fully Wednesday and Thursday but remains questionable. Shepherd has missed the Saints’ last two games while dealing with the illness. The Saints received encouraging news at linebacker, where Kaden Elliss and Anfernee Jennings both practiced fully Friday. Elliss has been working his way back from a calf injury, while Jennings has been dealing with a knee injury. Both are expected to be available against Pittsburgh. Kicker Daniel Carlson also returned to practice after missing the first two sessions for personal reasons. As he and his wife are still expecting the birth of their fourth child, Carlson traveled to France to rejoin the team and was a full participant Friday. With potentially challenging weather conditions including the chance for some rain and cross winds expected for the game, New Orleans will be glad to have the veteran specialist in tow Sunday. Running back Alvin Kamara remained limited with a back injury but was not assigned a game-status designation. Quarterback Tyler Shough, who has been managing a left-hand injury, practiced fully throughout the week. Other Saints listed as full participants Friday included running back C.J. Donaldson, cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry, quarterback Spencer Rattler, defensive lineman Davon Godchaux and offensive lineman Asim Richards, who was added to the report with a hand injury. Pittsburgh will be without wide receiver Ben Skowronek and cornerback Brandin Echols, both ruled out after missing practice throughout the week with calf and hamstring injuries, respectively. Running back Rico Dowdle and safety DeShon Elliott were listed as questionable. Dowdle was limited throughout the week with a knee injury after returning to action last Sunday, while Elliott participated fully in the first two sessions and was listed as a full participant for Friday’s estimated report. home.headline: ‘I Hate Poorly Ran Organizations’ — Former Steelers DT Slams Pittsburgh’s Questionable Travel Plan for Paris Game vs. Saints
home.blurb: In a scathing post on X, Fehoko pointed out the Saints’ opposite approach and slammed the Steelers, revealing that players did not sleep on overnight flights. “This is one of the dumbest things I’ve ever seen. Every NFL plane ride is pure card games, movie watching, and guys hanging out. Thinking that “they’ll sleep overnight” on the plane is so stupid. The Saints are already in Paris getting acclimated. I hate poorly ran organizations,” Fehoko wrote . The issue of different teams’ travel schedules reared its head when the Los Angeles Rams arrived in Australia less than 30 hours before kickoff, while the 49ers had arrived roughly a week earlier to acclimate. The 49ers look well rested as they blew out the sluggish Rams 27-7 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in front of 100,021 fans, the seventh-largest attendance in NFL history. The Pittsburgh Steelers improved to 4-2 on the season after a thrilling overtime 26-19 Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road. Next up, the Steelers will travel to Paris, France, for a Week 7 clash against the New Orleans Saints at Stade De France. Former Steelers defensive tackle Breiden Fehoko slammed the franchise after it was revealed that the team will take a red-eye flight to Paris on Thursday evening and go straight to training after landing. Breiden Fehoko Takes Issue With Steelers’ Paris Travel Plans PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Later, Rams coach Sean McVay took responsibility for the team’s unusual travel arrangements, while the 49ers were praised for adapting to the 17-hour time difference and acclimating more quickly. The 27-7 scoreline prompted the NFL to consider adopting a standardized travel timeline for international games, rather than leaving it to teams. The Steelers’ Week 7 clash against the Saints will also be held during a storm of protests that have gripped France in recent days. During this week’s segment of the “Christian Kuntz” podcast, Pittsburgh long snapper Christian Kuntz revealed that league officials had reassured the players of their safety during their stay in Paris. “We had an NFL security meeting. Which, I’m sure every team when you travel overseas, you have a meeting,” Kuntz said. “Basically, they told us that, ‘Yeah, there’s riots going on. This is why they’re rioting. It’s not a threat in our area. We have tripled the security now. Everything’s gonna be fine. Your families are gonna be safe.’ So, they’ve advised us that it’s gonna be safe.” The Steelers are seeking a third straight win after suffering a damaging Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns. Pittsburgh has shown flashes of brilliance on both sides of the ball this season, earning a PFN Team Impact score of 75.5 (No. 14 in the NFL). The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta. San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons. If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener. Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie. Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization. The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September. Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure. The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad . Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay. For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender. Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two. Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen. The 49ers (60%) pack their perfect record for a cross-country trip to face the Falcons in Week 7. My 49ers vs. Falcons predictions recognize that this is no normal road game for San Francisco, with a tough schedule spot threatening that undefeated mark. That angle informs my best NFL picks , starring Bijan Robinson, for Sunday, Oct. 25. 49ers vs Falcons prediction: Falcons moneyline We've seen a significant early market move toward the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. The San Francisco 49ers opened as 4.5-point road favorites following their win over Washington on Monday. Early opinions have trimmed as many as two points off that spread, pushing through the key number of 3. If you read my Week 7 NFL Underdogs column, you know I grabbed Atlanta +3.5 earlier in the week. With the Falcons now trading at +2.5, I see more worth in their outright price rather than taking less than a field goal (underdogs of +2.5 or shorter are 12-13 SU and ATS this season). On top of injuries stacking up for the 49ers, specifically at receiver, this venture to Georgia is just San Francisco's second true road game of the season. A good chunk of the Niners' positive power ratings are produced by those home-friendly results. This is also an early wake-up call for the 49ers, who take the field at 10 a.m. PT in Atlanta and do so on a short week , after playing on Monday in Week 6. There is also a looming look-ahead for a banged-up roster, with a bye waiting in Week 8. The Falcons are being downgraded for a sloppy loss to Chicago last weekend, in which Atlanta had three turnovers and less than 20 minutes of possession. Still, the Falcons were threatening a fourth-quarter. 49ers vs Falcons combo If you like a short underdog, often times the moneyline is worth a wager. Atlanta stays home while the 49ers travel for an early kickoff on a short week. The chairman of tight ends has scored five touchdowns and sees his role in the passing game spike with the Niners potentially down its top two WRs. Bijan Robinson is an underrated pass-catching threat and the Falcons need to get the ball in his hands by any means. Projections for Bijan flirt with as many as 40 receiving yards in Week 7. Falcons moneyline George Kittle touchdown Bijan Robinson 25+ receiving yards TOP PICK 49ers vs Falcons player prop: Bijan Robinson 25+ receiving yards The Falcons' path to victory is plowed by running back Bijan Robinson . Robinson isn't just a threat to grind out gains on the ground, but also is a catch-and-run weapon in this offense. Robinson did finish with negative receiving yards on just two catches in the loss to Chicago last Sunday, which is helping slim his yardage total for Week 7 (had 30.5 O/U in Week 6). The game before, however, he was targeted seven times for four grabs and 32 receiving yards . Robinson is a workhorse for Atlanta and could see an even bigger snap share with fellow RB Brian Robinson dealing with a hamstring injury. Week 7 projections for Robinson's receiving output all sit north of 30 yards, with a ceiling of 39. My number comes out to 33+ receiving yards. Want more NFL player props? LeBron's biggest comeback CBS Sports predicts close finish between Falcons, 49ers Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Atlanta Falcons have lost two straight games against tough teams - and it's not about to get any easier with the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers set to visit on Sunday afternoon. If nothing else this should be a good measuring-stick kind of game for the Falcons, where we'll get to find out just how far off they are from contending. For what it's worth, Pete Prisco at CBS Sports is expecting a close finish. He has Atlanta losing by just two points. "The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 If we knew how the Falcons could upset Kyle Shanahan's Niners we wouldn't be blogging about it, that's for sure. The last time these two teams met was almost exactly a year ago, and the 49ers came out on top, 20-10. Michael Penix threw for 241 yards and a touchdown and Mac Jones only threw for 152 yards, no touchdowns and a pick but the Niners wound the ground game handily. Bijan Robinson was limited to just 40 yards on 14 carries, while Christian McCaffrey racked up 129 yards on 24 attempts. Sunday's game starts at 1:00 p.m. ET at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. away.headline: 49ers injury updates: No major changes on 2nd week 7 practice report
away.blurb: There are a handful of players already ruled out for Week 7, but we could see some players back in action against the Falcons as the 49ers look to get a little healthier in time to go for a 7-0 start to the 2026 campaign. 49ers Week 7 injury report: Mike Evans among 6 ruled out It's not a surprise Evans is out while he deals with Achilles tendinitis, but Shanahan used the same language about the injury for Week 7 that he did leading up to Week 6 when Evans suited up despite not practicing. picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI I'm all about celebrating a win, but the Tennessee Titans are coming up on a must-win game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston (12) scores on a touchdown reception during the fourth quarter against New York Jets cornerback Brandon Stephens (21) at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. In front of a potentially revamped home crowd, the stars are aligning for a home upset for Tennessee. I don't believe the offense will take any major strides, but in Week 7, maybe they won't have to. I predict a narrow Titans win over the Browns. Published Oct 21, 2026 LANE MILLS Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 2 TRENDING World Series preview NFL injury updates Knicks change ring tune Cowboys not trading? LeBron's biggest comeback 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jimmy Morris Fri, October 23, 2026 at 3:51 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This matchup between the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans looks to be the most boring game of the week. The total in this game currently sits at 37.5 over at FanDuel Sportsbook . That is the lowest total of the week, and the under might be the smart bet. The Titans are last in the league in yards per game at 236.3. The Browns are 29th at 267.5. Get ready for a lot of punts. The key for the Titans in this game will be taking care of the ball. Last week, the Titans forced three turnovers against the Indianapolis Colts. That, and a couple of key special teams plays, were the difference in the game. This game will likely play out in a similar way. Speaking of special teams plays, it was really good to see Chimere Dike break off a 58-yard punt return against the Colts. Dike was the biggest weapon the Titans had last season, but he had struggled this season before last week. Hopefully, that was the start of his return to the All-Pro returner he was last season. This game does feature two good rookie wide receivers. Denzel Boston leads all rookie receivers with 345 yards and is averaging over 20 yards per catch. Carnell Tate is right behind him with 344 yards. If one of those guys can break a big play, it could be the difference in this game. Don't expect a thrilling game when you sit down to watch this one on Sunday, but if the Titans can play a game similar to the one they did last week, they might have a chance at back-to-back wins for the first time since 2022.

away.headline: Final Injury Report: Who's In and Out for Titans vs. Browns
away.blurb: Final Injury Report: Who's In and Out for Titans vs. Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Final Injury Report: Who's In and Out for Titans vs. Browns The stage is set, and here's what we know about the Titans' injuries going into the game. No players are listed out, but there will be plenty of game-time decisions. Tony Adams, Dorian Mausi, Calvin Ridley, Tyjae Spears and Kevin Winston Jr. were all questionable on the final injury report . Head coach Robert Saleh said at his Friday presser that the team wasn't ruling anyone out. A few players still need to be cleared, but Saleh said everyone was trending in the right direction. His playing time on Sunday will depend on Winston's status. Winston missed the last game with a quad injury. The second-year safety was limited the first two days but returned to full participation on Friday. Then, there's the potential return of linebacker Dorian Mausi. Mausi has missed the season so far with a foot injury and has been designated for return. The Titans activated Joshua Williams from the PUP list last week, so we'll see if the same happens for Mausi. Ridley was limited on Wednesday and Thursday and didn't practice on Friday. As we've seen a lot this season, Spears has been dealing with a knee injury. However, it hasn't kept him out of a game yet. Expect Spears to play on Sunday unless there is a major setback. F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 2 (DENNY SIMMONS / THE TENNESSEAN) Grant Bricker Fri, October 23, 2026 at 8:54 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Tennessee Titans look to stack another win this weekend with the Cleveland Browns coming to town. The Titans are fresh off their first win of the season with a thrilling 26-20 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6. The team is back home for the first time in two weeks and is still searching for its first home win of the year. The Browns are 4-1 in their last five games and currently led the AFC North. Adams has filled in at safety for the Titans lately. He stepped in when Amani Hooker went down with a concussion and missed the Week 5 game against the Houston Texans. Adams is dealing with an ankle injury. The only day of practice that Adams was a full participant was Friday. In the games he's played in, Adams has been very productive. He has accounted for a combined 21 total tackles, one sack and one TFL in the last two games. Mausi practiced fully every day this week and, at a minimum, could provide valuable depth. away.headline: Browns new star RB trade target emerges amid injury trouble
away.blurb: The Cleveland Browns are having a good start to the season, as they have a 4-2 record and are at the top of the AFC North. With the way the Browns are playing, it is very likely that they will be buyers ahead of the trade deadline. When looking at the Browns’ current roster, it is clear that they should be looking to add a running back. They have been dealing with injury trouble at the position, so it would not be surprising at all if they acquired a running back by the deadline. Due to this, the Browns are now being connected to a notable running back trade candidate. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Browns as the top potential suitor for Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. “Running back Tony Pollard is a good support piece for Ward right now, but he’s 29 years old and an impending free agent. He should have a solid trade market, though, as he has four 1,000-yard seasons on his resume and could upgrade several of the backfields that have been impacted by injuries this season,” Knox wrote. “Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Seattle Seahawks.” Pollard would certainly be an interesting running back for the Browns to add to their roster as they continue their playoff push. The eight-year NFL veteran would provide Cleveland’s offense with a nice boost, as he is still an impactful player at this stage in his career. In six games this season with the Titans, Pollard has recorded one touchdown, 87 rushes, and 349 rushing yards. He also recorded over 1,000 rushing yards over his previous four seasons. With this, the Pro Bowler would be a significant pickup for the Browns if acquired. It will be interesting to see if they pursue him because of it. home.headline: What Robert Saleh said about Jordan Elliott situation, response from Titans and NFL
home.blurb: "The (defensive line) room is really close," Saleh said. "For JFM to go out there and kind of help Jordan through with whatever he was dealing with at that moment I thought was really admirable on JFM’s part." The incident, which is under review by the NFL, followed a practice altercation with teammate JC Latham. Teammate John Franklin-Myers was credited with de-escalating the situation before it worsened. Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed on Oct. 21 that Jordan Elliott pulled a gun in the team facility's parking lot after a practice altercation last week, leading to the defensive tackle's release this week. An NFL spokesperson told The Tennessean on Oct. 21 that the Titans "promptly" notified the league about the matter, and it is under review. Saleh praised the organization and the NFL's response to the incident, citing a "pause" by the team and the league in getting Elliott assistance for what Saleh called a sign for "a cry for help" instead of involving law enforcement. "And the reason why I think the NFL and the organization did an outstanding job is because this is a man who is father, a great husband. He’s never committed a crime in his entire life," Saleh said. "And he pulled a gun in the parking lot. And the first question that I think everyone forgets to ask is why would a great man, a great father, a man who shows up on time every day, works his ass off every day, contributes the way he's supposed to contribute, is well-liked in the locker room — Why did he go off the rails and grab a gun? "And to me, those are small signs of a cry of help. In terms of, obviously there’s something greater happening. And I thought the team and the NFL did an outstanding job with regards to pausing and asking those questions and checking every single box with regards to getting him the help that he needs." Saleh vouched for Elliott's character despite the incident. The veteran defensive tackle with seven seasons in the NFL played for Saleh in San Francisco last year before joining the Titans in free agency in the spring. "These kids go through a lot. A lot. And... I will stand on the table for Jordan’s character," Saleh said. "Unfortunately, rules are rules with regards to guns on property. And sometimes it’s far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they are down. "My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a helluva run-stopping defensive tackle that can help you on a playoff run, give me a call. I’ll tell you everything you need to know about him. He’s a good man. Had a terrible lapse in judgement that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act." What happened with Jordan Elliott at the Titans' facility? Elliott attempted to retrieve a gun from his vehicle after a practice altercation with JC Latham on Oct. 15, according to multiple reports. On the other hand, the Colts fell to 2-4 last week with an upset loss to the previously winless Titans. It was their second straight loss after a 34-22 defeat in Pittsburgh on Oct. 11. Colts vs. Vikings Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: I'm starting to think the Colts are a bottom-three team in the NFL, but people haven't realized it yet. Heading into Week 7, they're 31st in net yards per play (-1.3), 21st in EPA per play, and 28th in opponent EPA per play. Their only redeeming quality has been Jonathan Taylor. If it wasn't for JT, their offensive numbers would be in the bottom five as well. If I close my eyes and think about this matchup, all I can envision is the Vikings' defense living in the Colts' backfield. Not only are they going to blitz Daniel Jones into oblivion, but they also lead the league in both opponent rush EPA and opponent rush success rate, meaning they're perfectly equipped to stop the one weapon Indianapolis has. They’ve lost two games in a row, including last week to the lowly Titans, and now have a road matchup against an undefeated team off their bye week. picks.headline: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions as Kyle Murray & Co. Host the Colts in Week 7
picks.source: Minnesota Vikings On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: The Vikings will host a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday for just the third time this season as they welcome the 2-4 Colts to the Twin Cities in Week 7 . Minnesota looks to remain undefeated coming off an early Week 6 bye, while Indy will be scratching to salvage a start that has already led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard . Needless to say, these are two teams currently heading in completely different directions. With a beast of a November schedule looming, here are my predictions for a Vikings team looking to put together a dominating performance. 1. Kyler Murray will rack up 300-plus yards between the air and ground While the early bye provided desperately needed injury relief for the Vikings, there are fair concerns that the break may have disrupted the progress Kyler Murray and the passing game were starting to make. Murray’s performance in New Orleans was especially promising, mainly due to the fact that the offense entered the game without wideout Jordan Addison and left tackle Christian Darrisaw, and then lost tight end T.J. Hockenson to a concussion early. With all three looking to return this weekend, I see Murray having his best day yet in purple. Indy’s 351.2 yards allowed per game rank ninth in the league, and Murray’s abilities through the air and on the ground make him especially hard to stop (h/t: Ian Hartitz). After totaling 280 total yards against the Saints (229 passing, 51 rushing), I predict Murray will finish with over 300 total yards on Sunday. 2. Vikings' offense explodes for over 30 points The Vikings’ season started with a bang, scoring 39 points in the season opener against the Packers. Since then, they have not scored more than 23 points in a game. Sunday is the perfect opportunity for that to change. The Colts have given up 27.3 points per game so far this season, the sixth-highest average in the league. Minnesota, meanwhile, is looking for its first truly dominant offensive showing as it prepares for the hardest stretch of its schedule. The returns of Hockenson and Addison should open up passing options, and Jordan Mason’s possible return to the backfield could elevate a run game that Aaron Jones has carried almost entirely on his own so far. The Vikings’ offense needs to prove it can score consistently before facing some of the league's toughest opponents, and the Colts’ shaky defense may give them plenty of opportunities. 3. Harrison Smith wakes up and snags his 40th career interception Franchise legend Harrison Smith has had a relatively quiet start to his 15th NFL season . Smith announced his return a week before the Vikings kicked off their 2026 campaign and has mostly been a rotational piece in defensive coordinator Brian Flores’s ever-evolving defense. Even though “The Hitman” is clearly past his prime, he’s still one of the smartest defenders in the game, and I expect that to pay off this weekend. Smith recently confirmed to Richard Sherman that this will be his last season , so there is no better time to snag his 40th interception than now (h/t: "Richard Sherman Podcast"). Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has thrown six interceptions this season, tied for the third-most in the league , and anyone who's watched him through his career knows he’ll eventually throw a duck or two (h/t: NFL). Smith’s football IQ and Jones’s occasional recklessness may just be the perfect combination to get the NFL’s active interception leader his next pick. Since Week 14 of the 2025 season, the Vikings have won 10 straight games, building a 5-0 record going into last week's bye. They face a 2-4 Indianapolis team that fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Head coach Shane Steichen is still employed , but the Colts feel combustible right now, with rumors of trading away star players like RB Jonathan Taylor and G Quenton Nelson swirling. Minnesota can't afford to overlook Indianapolis if they want to keep pace with the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. But this feels like an opportunity for the Vikings to jump on an inferior team that is going through organizational changes. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings when they host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday. Jordan Mason will run for 100+ yards and 2 touchdowns Jordan Mason appears to return to the lineup after missing the past four games with a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen on Tuesday that he expects to see Mason, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Christian Darrisaw back at practice on Wednesday . With Mason back, Minnesota can return to its 1-2 punch with Aaron Jones. Indianapolis enters Week 7 as one of the league's worst run defenses. away.blurb: Coming out of their bye week, the Vikings have almost a perfectly clean injury report as they head into the weekend preparing to host the Colts on Sunday at U.S. Bank Stadium. The Indianapolis Colts will miss a star player on each side of the football for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. Warren hasn't practiced all week after missing a Week 6 loss to the Tennessee Titans with a groin injury. Steichen said Wednesday that the 24-year-old was "progressing well" in his recovery. Despite missing Sunday's game, Warren still leads the Colts with 30 catches. The former Penn State star began his second NFL season with touchdowns in back-to-back games but has tallied 213 yards, dropping his average yards per catch to 7.1 from 10.8 in his rookie campaign. Will Mallory played his first game of the season in Warren's absence, collecting two catches for 20 yards. Mo Alie-Cox turned his only touch into a 1-yard touchdown, but Daniel Jones didn't target Andrew Ogletree once in 30 snaps. "I'm not really concerned," Gardner said Wednesday, per Colts.com's JJ Stankevitz . "I trust our training staff here, and like I said, it's not as bad as last year. I'm just happy that it's not the same spot." The timing is still rough for the Colts ahead of a matchup against star Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson. Yet Gardner has struggled this season, with Pro Football Focus noting that he's allowed the most yards per reception (21.7) of any cornerback. The short-handed Colts will look to hand the Vikings their first loss of the season this Sunday. The Week 7 clash starts at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

home.headline: Vikings-Colts Second Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they had some players upgraded and one added- linebacker CJ Allen. But starters Sauce Gardner, Tyler Warren, and Rigoberto Sanchez did not practice for a second straight day on Thursday, making their availability on Sunday increasingly doubtful. The Jets are early 4.5-point favorites, but the Dolphins' improving rushing attack creates room for several bold predictions. Ollie Gordon II will rush for at least 100 yards. Gordon has totaled 188 yards in two starts since De'Von Achane went on injured reserve. Miami's 217-yard performance against Cincinnati should convince the coaching staff to keep the offense on the ground. New York has been much stronger against the pass than the run, which gives Gordon a favorable path to volume. Malik Willis will produce two touchdowns and no more than one turnover. This is the prediction that would change the game. Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble against Cincinnati, but the bye gives Miami time to reduce his difficult reads. Designed runs and play-action can turn his mobility into production while limiting risky throws. Miami will record at least three sacks. The Dolphins have only four sacks through five games, making this the boldest defensive call. Hafley's staff has two weeks to design pressure packages against Geno Smith. A healthier edge rotation and more aggressive use of linebackers could finally create the disruption missing against Cincinnati. The game will be decided by three points or fewer. The early total sits below 40 at several books. New York averages 18.6 points and Miami 14. The Jets have the stronger defense, while the Dolphins have the more productive recent running game. Neither team has shown enough passing explosiveness to create confidence in a runaway. A reasonable projection is Jets 20, Dolphins 17, but that margin leaves the upset door open. If Miami wins the turnover battle, Gordon controls the tempo and special teams avoid another disastrous start, the Dolphins can reverse the score. Bold predictions are not promises. They are matchup-based possibilities. The first three require Miami to emerge from the bye with a more disciplined offense and a more creative defense. If those changes appear, the fourth prediction should follow naturally.

Miami's immediate focus is to put together a full game and turn flashes of competitiveness into consistency. The longer-term focus has the coaching staff and front office considering which players from this rebuild will remain with the team in 2027 and beyond. Miami has 22 players on expiring contracts this season, and Miami Dolphins on SI writer Alain Poupart took a look at who could be playing themselves into a contract extension as well as players who are likely to hit the free agent market after the season. For the four most likely free agents to return, Poupart starts with a veteran at a position everyone expected to be a weak point for the Dolphins this season: CB JuJu Brents — This is a player the Dolphins should prioritize because he still continues to perform at a high level and plays a premium position. The ability to stay healthy has been the issue so far in Brents' career, but he hasn't missed a game yet (knock on wood) so far in 2026. As for a player who might be allowed to leave in free agency, Poupart started his list of four with a name many fans could have guessed: T Austin Jackson — Despite his poor Pro Football Focus standing (he's dead last among all NFL tackles), Jackson is a solid veteran tackle who's simply off to a bad start. The issue with Jackson is how it would cost to bring him back in what probably wouldn't be a starting role and whether he even would be interested in that idea after being asked to take a pay cut this year.
