away.headline: Gordon, Bell make interesting admissions. And Dolphins injury, ownership news
away.blurb: Bell, who has five catches for 92 yards in five games and three starts, has played only 34 snaps with Caleb Douglas, who’s due to return Sunday after missing three games with an ankle injury. “I can’t wait to be playing with him on Sunday,” Bell said. ▪ For the Dolphins on Sunday at the Jets, linebacker Willie Gay Jr. (illness) and safety Kyle Louis (knee) are listed as questionable; defensive end Rob Beal (hamstring) is doubtful and cornerback Reese Taylor (quadriceps) is out. Gay said Friday that he’s feeling better and expects to play on Sunday. Other than Gay, Beal and Taylor, nobody else on the 53-man roster has an injury designation. Receiver Caleb Douglas is set to return after missing three games with an ankle injury. Jets running back Breece Hall is listed as questionable with a quadriceps injury. ▪ Even when the Dolphins released kicker Zane Gonzalez with an injury settlement on Aug. 19, he knew there was a chance he could return. ▪ In one year, Ollie Gordon II has gone from producing one of the NFL’s lowest per-carry averages (2.8) to one of the highest (5.0). But if you ask him the reason for his improvement, he doesn’t mention what a lot of running backs would likely say – that it’s easier to be successful when you receive a steady workload and can get into a rhythm. Instead, Gordon offered this explanation during a conversation at his locker this week: “I feel like I practice a lot harder than I did my rookie year,” he said. “It was so embedded into our brains this year [to] finish runs. It’s an everyday thing, It’s non-negotiable. That’s one of those things where it’s like, I’ve got to do it so we’re going to get it done.” That speaks well of new running backs coach Ladell Betts. It also is anecdotal evidence of how a new coaching staff sometimes can instill a sense of urgency in players that wasn’t necessarily there before. Everyone can relate to trying to impress the new boss. And as one Dolphins defensive veteran said, players listen more to Jeff Hafley than they did to Mike McDaniel during McDaniel’s final year as coach. Asked if he has changed his running style in any way to mirror what he accomplished at Oklahoma State (where he led FBS in rushing yards in his second season), Gordon said he has been “more decisive” and “not overthinking it” when he gets the ball. Only five players with at least 40 carries have averaged more yards per rush than Gordon, who has scampered for 5.0 yards per run on 47 attempts. Only eight running backs with at least as many carries have averaged more yards after contact than Gordon’s 3.38. In fairness to Gordon, his 2.8 per-carry average last season was skewed somewhat by the fact that many of his runs were short-yardage attempts against eight- or nine-man fronts, some in goal-line situations. ▪ Receiver Chris Bell — who has no receptions the past two games — also made a couple of interesting admissions on Friday. away.headline: Miami Dolphins injury report: Rookie WR Caleb Douglas back for Jets
away.blurb: Douglas had been out since Week 2 when he suffered a sprained ankle against the San Francisco 49ers. Despite missing the last three games for 0-5 Miami, Douglas leads the Dolphins with 56.5 reception yards per game. Linebacker Willie Gay was ill and missed Thursday's practice. Hafley said he was feeling better on Friday morning and was limited at practice in the afternoon. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's game. Promising rookie safety/linebacker Kyle Louis has been on the Physically Unable to Perform list since injuring his knee in the season-opener at Las Vegas. Hafley said he wants to wait until Friday's practice to determine if Louis will be activated. He is listed as questionable for Sunday. The Jets likely will be missing LB Kiko Mauigo (quad), OL Max Mitchel (concussion), RB Kene Nwangwu (knee) and EDGE Joseph Ossai (ankle), who all did not practice on Thursday. "Caleb will play," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said at his Friday press conference. Meanwhile, quarterback Malik Willis, who did not throw during the bye week with an injured right thumb, has been practicing and is good to go. Hafley said running back Jaylen Wright (foot) will play. Tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring) said Thursday that he's good to go. "He has stayed sharp but you're talking about a rookie who hasn't played much football," Hafley said. One new face Dolphins fans will see Sunday is placekicker Zane Gonzalez. Hafley talked about Gonzalez replacing Riley Patterson as the team's placekicker earlier in the week. He said it wasn't meant as a message. "We felt it was best for our team going forward," Hafley said. "Zane did a great job when he was here and then he was injured." home.headline: Caleb Douglas could return to Miami Dolphins lineup against New York Jets
home.blurb: “Caleb will be limited [in practice] today. You know, we’ll see how he looks today and progress to Wednesday, but I think there’s optimism there. Let’s see how it goes today, and if he can get ramped up on Wednesday, it would be good to get him back out there.” The Miami Dolphins had a much needed bye week this past weekend. Multiple players have been banged up, including standout rookie receiver Caleb Douglas. It seems the added rest has been a good thing for the young pass catcher, as according to head coach Jeff Hafley, Douglas has a chance to suit up against the New York Jets on the road this upcoming Sunday. During his press availability on Monday morning, head coach Jeff Hafley was asked about Douglas’ potential to practice this week. Hafley, with a smile on his face, would go on to speak about what Miami missed on offense without Douglas in the mix. “Just kind of looking back through the last couple of weeks, some of the things that he did, we’ve missed him. And to see a rookie kind of have to start and stop like that, not ideal. But, he’s worked really hard and it would be very great to get him back.” We will keep a close eye on Douglas’ practice participation as the week unfolds, but as of Monday afternoon, his availability seems to be pointing in a positive direction in regards to playing this Sunday.

Prisco picked a one-point Panthers win, saying, "The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. His CBS colleague John Breech is also picking the Panthers, but he's taking them by a field goal. SI's Ian MacMillan isn't buying any of what the Panthers are doing, and he's picking the Buccaneers to upset them in Charlotte. "Time to sell high on [the Panthers]. They were favored last time out on the road against the Philadelphia Eagles, but only after some late injury updates for Philly. This week, they're headed back home to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in an early-season rivalry bout. While the Buccaneers are struggling at the bottom of the division, these matchups are always tough and important. So, what do the odds tell us this week? Panthers favored against Buccaneers for now Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) plays against the Philadelphia Eagles | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Panthers open as 3.5-point favorites at home ( FanDuel ) over the Buccaneers. The Panthers open as 3.5-point favorites at home ( FanDuel ) over the Buccaneers. One could argue that the spread is a little too small given the trajectory of the two franchises and the most recent outings for both. Regardless, the Panthers are favored at home. They're -105 to cover the spread, while the Buccaneers are -115 to cover. That's also a little bit interesting. The Panthers have won three contests by an average of 16 points. The Panthers are -180 on the moneyline, so they are expected to win outright. The Buccaneers are +152 to win. The over/under is set at 44.5, and the over and under are both currently set at -110. So, based on that, the oddsmakers expect the Panthers to win a tight contest, 24-21. In other words, the Panthers are not expected to blow out a 1-5 team at home. Now, there is a huge caveat to these odds and what they're telling us. Right now, it is totally up in the air as to which QB the Panthers will see. away.headline: ‘He shouldn’t be playing,’ ‘It always goes horribly wrong’ — NFL fans push back on Buccaneers’ decision to start Baker Mayfield despite injury
away.blurb: Baker Mayfield’s expected return has some Buccaneers fans asking for another week of patience. The protective glove on his throwing hand isn’t doing much to settle their nerves. Todd Bowles said Friday that Mayfield is expected to start after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb. He remained listed as questionable despite practicing fully all three days this week. “Maybe wait 1 more week? We’re inventing new glove technology so that he can return early with an injured throwing thumb to a 1-5 team?” the fan wrote . The team’s practice reports provide some encouraging evidence for the return. Fans remain concerned about how those throws will translate once Carolina’s defense gets involved. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are preparing to get their starting quarterback back against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. At 1-5, however, some supporters question whether bringing him back now is worth it. Baker Mayfield Expected To Start Against Carolina Panthers Mayfield suffered the throwing-hand injury against Minnesota in Week 3 . Rookie Jalon Daniels has handled the starting job during his absence. The glove has become a focal point of the comeback discussion. According to the Buccaneers’ account of his preparation , it provides support to prevent the injured ligament from bending backward. Mayfield also acknowledged adjusting his release points because the glove changes his grip. That detail prompted one fan to question the urgency. Another supporter made a similar argument using Tampa Bay’s record. “Its easier to rest him another week we are 1 and [expletive] 5 theres genuinely no rush if he’s not 100%,” the supporter wrote . Fans Worry About Another Mayfield Comeback Through Injury One commenter greeted the news with sarcasm. “The Baker Mayfield playing hurt gimmick is back. Should go well just like it always does!” the fan wrote . The same user later clarified the criticism. “You’ve got me all wrong here, I agree he is hurt, the ‘gimmick’ is he always plays through injuries and it always goes horribly wrong,” the commenter added . Fantasy analyst Ian Hartitz also sounded unconvinced by the glove solution. “No reason to worry here. They ripped off one of the glove’s fingers! He’s fine! Everything is fine,” Hartitz wrote sarcastically . One fan expressed concern , writing, “So his throwing hand isn’t 100% healthy, which means he shouldn’t be playing.” Another fan imagined Carolina’s defenders enjoying the matchup. “Devin Lloyd and Will Lee stretching for some pick sixes this week,” the fan joked . PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Mayfield currently ranks 33rd in PFN’s NFL QB Impact rankings with a 63.1 grade across three appearances. He has thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. Tampa Bay needs more from its offense, and Mayfield’s full practice week gives Bowles reason for optimism. away.headline: Is Baker Mayfield playing this week? Injury update for Buccaneers QB
away.blurb: Bowles indicated that Mayfield would return as the Buccaneers' starter in their Week 7 matchup with the Carolina Panthers . Baker Mayfield (questionable – thumb) The Buccaneers only have two quarterbacks on their active roster in Week 7 as Mayfield is expected to return despite his official designation as questionable. Daniels, the undrafted free agent rookie who filled in for the veteran for three starts, will return to his role as backup after leading the Bucs to a 1-2 record. The good news keeps coming for Tampa Bay fans. On the same day the Rays are set to begin their second World Series appearance this decade, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers also announced Friday, Oct. 23 they're getting back quarterback Baker Mayfield . Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles told reporters that Mayfield worked through a regular string of practices in Week 7 and that the quarterback "looks like he's ready to go." The Bucs' starter has missed three games since he dislocated the thumb on his right (throwing) hand late in the fourth quarter of a Sept. 27 clash with the Minnesota Vikings . From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. JALON DANIELS: What to know about rookie filling in for Baker Mayfield Bowles said after the quarterback's diagnosis at the time that he'd miss at least three weeks with the injury. Reports emerged in Week 5 indicating that Mayfield wanted to beat the three-week timeline , but he did not participate in any practices for the last three weeks. Things changed for the better for Mayfield this week – Tampa Bay listed him as a full participant in every practice on its Week 7 injury report. Here's what to know ahead of the Buccaneers' meeting with the Panthers: Is Baker Mayfield playing this week? The 31-year-old quarterback was a full participant in practice every day this week after missing three games (and nine practices) with a dislocated thumb. Mayfield said he's been wearing a glove on his right hand to help protect his thumb from taking more hits in practice. "(It's) not restricting because it's on the back side. The trainers and equipment staff did an incredible job. I mean, they even went to somebody that works with the Rays to be able to work on something specific that they've done in the past," Mayfield said. "For me, just getting used to it. I don't feel the difference. It's just like me wearing a glove." Tampa Bay also has two quarterbacks on its practice squad: Easton Stick, who served as Daniels' backup for the last three weeks, and Brett Rypien. away.blurb: How Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield got help from Tampa Bay Rays on return from thumb injury | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Baker Mayfield is set to come back, which is a huge boost for the Buccaneers. But his return from a thumb injury isn't so simple. With his thumb injury being on his throwing hand, playing quarterback might be a bit tricky. But he recently got some help. Rays helped Baker Mayfield with custom glove amid return from thumb injury While the Rays are focused on winning the World Series, Bond was able to help out the city's NFL team by designing a new glove to help Mayfield play through a thumb injury. According to Rick Stroud of The Tampa Bay Times , the Tampa Bay Rays actually helped design a new custom glove for Mayfield's right hand leading up to Week 7 to try to help him play without any complications. "Baker Mayfield will wear a glove on his right hand with a solid plate on the back to keep his once-dislocated thumb from bending the wrong way when he likely starts Sunday's game at Carolina," Stroud writes. away.headline: Buccaneers Week 7 injury report: Mayfield returns, Egbuka sidelined
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers received encouraging news Wednesday as Baker Mayfield returned to full participation in practice after missing three games with a right thumb injury. However, wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was among five players who did not practice as Tampa Bay prepares for Sunday's NFC South matchup against the Carolina Panthers . Luke Goedeke (calf), Bucky Irving (illness), Zyon McCollum (illness) and Christian Rozeboom (finger) also missed practice. Antoine Winfield Jr. was limited with a rib injury, while Sean Tucker and Cody Mauch participated fully. Carolina quarterback Bryce Young fully participated despite a knee injury, while running back Chuba Hubbard was held out for rest. Practice designations: FP = Full Participation; LP = Limited Participation; DNP = Did Not Participate. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. home.headline: Panthers HC Dave Canales provides encouraging updates on CBs Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson
home.blurb: Head coach Dave Canales spoke with reporters following this afternoon's practice, just ahead of their upcoming bout against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . He was asked about the progress of corners Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, who have been on injured reserve for the past few weeks. "Jaycee is doing great," Canales stated. "The reports I get are that he's trending in the right direction—ahead of whatever general deadlines. He's crushing his rehab right now. He's itching to just keep taking the next step. "Mike Jack, same thing. He's moving around, they're starting to pick up their speeds, the change-of-direction stuff. Those are all the things, with the nature of the injuries that have to feel really good before you're able to open up. Obviously, we gotta go through the four games. And then, after that, you start thinking about opening up windows." Both Horn (quad) and Jackson (groin) went down during the team's Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns . Initial reports suggested that Horn would be in danger of missing the remainder of the campaign while Jackson was expected back some time in November. Carolina, in their places, have started rookie Will Lee III and special teams ace Akayleb Evans. Follow @ThePanthersWire on Twitter/X for more Panthers content. Meanwhile, Cincy is coming out of a bye week and is in a prime spot to make a run up the AFC North standings. After this game, the Bengals take on Tennessee, Atlanta, Pittsburgh, Washington and New Orleans (four teams under .500) to close out October and November. After missing the playoffs last season, Cincy is hoping a healthy Burrow is enough to make a playoff run in 2026. Plus, we may hit an exact score along the way. This AFC North matchup is one of the biggest games in Week 7, and I think there’s a chance we’ll see an upset with Cincy coming out of a bye. Here’s my score prediction for Sunday’s contest. Baltimore opened as a 3-point favorite , but the Bengals were favored on Wednesday after Jackson was limited in practice. The total has moved down from 50.5 to 48.5. Bengals vs. Ravens Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking the Bengals to cover on the road: As I've written about already in this article, this is the week when I really start looking at strength of schedule, betting against teams who have had it easy through the first six weeks and betting on teams who have had it tough. No one has had it easier than the Baltimore Ravens, who have started their season against the Colts, Saints, Cowboys, Titans, Falcons, and Browns. Now they'll face their best competition yet, the Bengals, who are going to be feeling fresh off their bye. Lamar Jackson's status for this game is up in the air, but we can assume, based on the betting line, that the market believes he'll play. If he does sit out, we're going to end up with a great line with Cincinnati +3. The Bengals are seventh in EPA per play and 13th in opponent EPA per play while playing a much more difficult schedule than the Ravens. I think they can at least keep this game within a field goal, if not win it outright. Jackson’s status obviously could swing this game, but the Ravens haven’t exactly had to face a tough path in the 2026 season. Meanwhile, Cincy is coming out of a bye and is ninth in the NFL in EPA/Play on offense. Burrow and Co. should make things tough on a Ravens team that struggled a bit against Atlanta and wasn’t able to come up with enough stops in losses to New Orleans and Cleveland. The margin for error for the Ravens becomes much thinner if Jackson doesn’t play, or if he’s not 100 percent. I like Cincy to get an upset win on Sunday. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week after missing all three of the team's practices ahead of Week 6. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. Minter: Lamar Jackson (ankle) could "potentially" practice this week. Remains day-to-day. Minter's update on Jackson isn't viewed as a positive one in the betting market. Ahead of Week 7, oddsmakers set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Bengals. Now, DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set as a 2.5-point favorite, though it remains -148 on the moneyline to win this game. It's not a major adjustment, but clearly there is some worry that Jackson could miss his third game in a row. Currently, DraftKings has received 73 percent of the moneyline bets in this game on the Bengals to win outright. After going down against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, Jackson has not played. He missed a win over Atlanta in Week 5 and a loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. The Cleveland loss looms large for the Ravens, as they are now behind the Browns in the AFC North standings. The Ravens are a much more dangerous team with Jackson in the lineup, and he was an MVP candidate before going down in Week 4. This season, the star quarterback has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. A two-time MVP, Jackson leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Tyler Huntley would receive the start in Week 7 if Jackson can't go. Dating back to last season, the Ravens are 3-1 in Huntley's last four starts, but they remain 7-12 all-time when Jackson is sidelined. Huntley struggled to move the offense in Week 6, throwing for 165 yards and a score in a 13-10 loss. He did combine for three scores in the win over Atlanta, so there is a higher ceiling that what he showed this past Sunday. If Jackson doesn't practice on Wednesday, it's possible this line could move even further towards the Bengals. For now, oddsmakers are still giving the Ravens the edge in this divisional battle. Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson did get in some “limited” work today. https://t.co/3rq60qmJVB The Ravens opened as three-point favorites at home in this massive Week 7 matchup against AFC North foe, and that line bounced around from 2.5 to 3 in the lead up to Wednesday's practice. However, Jackson was not spotted at the beginning of practice and was later seen walking off with a limp. As a result, oddsmakers at DraftKings quickly shifted the odds in this game to Bengals -1.5, a huge 4.5-point flip from where they were entering the week. Lamar Jackson (ankle) seen walking off practice field with a limp, per @CordellWoodland . https://t.co/1R708hsFHo That's a sign that Jackson isn't expected to play in Week 7, and he may need to log a full practice on Thursday or Friday to shift the sentiment in the betting market. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers this week about how they set the line for a game like this with Jackson's status up in the air. "Your lookahead line, you essentially have to assume he's going to play until you hear otherwise.," Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. "So, that's baked into the price, whether we anticipate he'll be at full strength or 80% strength, that would kind of be factored in there. "And then, as the week goes on, we'll adjust as we know more. Obviously, he wasn't at practice today, and our line went down a point and a half just off that alone. And then we'll kind of trickle down as the week goes on and his status becomes more and more certain one way or the other. If he's back at practice tomorrow in a limited or full capacity, the line will probably shift back towards the Ravens. If he's not there again on Thursday, we'll essentially start pricing as though [Tyler] Huntley is going to be the starter." So, what could the line close at if Huntley makes his third start in a row? "If he's out and it's Huntley again, the line will most likely shift to the Bengals being the favorite, probably in that 1.5 to 2.5 range," Gour said. So, based on Gour's projection, the current line suggest that Jackson won't play. That would be a huge blow to a Ravens team that is 4-2 and already lost a division game in Week 6. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score while leading the NFL in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating. The Ravens are 7-12 all time without Jackson, though they've won three of the four starts Huntley has made in his place since the 2025 season. Bettors are going to want to monitor Baltimore's practice report on Thursday, as it could solidify Jackson's status for Sunday's game. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. LeBron's biggest comeback Bengals vs. Ravens bold predictions for AFC North clash in Week 7 Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:21 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Cincinnati Bengals , Ja'Marr Chase saved some money by appealing. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. One of his teammates is anticipating a great game from him. Joe Burrow looking forward to facing Trey Hendrickson Burrow has practiced against Hendrickson many a time over the years, but the two have never been opponents in a real game before. There's no confusion on what he's expecting from No. 91, now in purple instead of orange. "It'll be fun, it'll be fun," Burrow said of seeing Hendrickson rushing at him . "I got to practice with him for a long time, and I'm sure he's excited to hit me a little bit after not hitting me for so long. It'll be fun." Hendrickson experienced the best years of his career on the team Burrow quarterbacked. The two nearly won a Super Bowl together, and almost made it back to another one a year later. Those memories are now an afterthought with undeniably high stakes in this matchup. The Bengals would like to avoid an 0-2 start in AFC North play. A loss would also drop them back to .500 at 3-3 overall. The Ravens just lost to the Cleveland Browns, and a second straight divisional defeat would set them back as well. How effectively Burrow evades his former teammate may determine the outcome in this game. Simpson is expecting greatness in Hendrickson's first chance at revenge, but Cincinnati is also looking for validation in moving on from the four-time Pro Bowler. They'll undoubtedly receive it if Burrow leaves the game untouched and standing. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Lamar Jackson Reveals Severity of Ankle Injury, Latest on QB's Status for Ravens vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Jackson had gone through "a good couple of days" since rejoining practice in a limited capacity this week for the first time since Week 4. The ankle injury forced Jackson to miss the last two games, and Baltimore has gone 1-1 during that stretch. He reportedly had a chance to play in the Ravens' Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, but ultimately wasn't ready to return as Baltimore lost 13-10. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson says he is "heading in the right direction" and could play in Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after returning to practice earlier this week. "I can't call it right now. Still got a grace period. We'll see, man. Hopefully," Jackson said Friday. "But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now." "It's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective... he feels like he can be," Minter said (h/t ESPN's Jamison Hensley). After avoiding injuries through the first three games of the season, Jackson exited the Ravens' Week 4 game against the Tennessee Titans due to an ankle injury. In four games, Jackson has thrown for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, adding 144 yards and a score on the ground. The Ravens are sitting at 4-2 on the season heading into this week's matchup against the Bengals. Tyler Huntley has filled in for Jackson in his absence and has collected 429 passing yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions. Injuries have unfortunately been the story for Jackson over the last two seasons. He missed four games last year and finished the 2025 campaign with 2,549 passing yards, 21 touchdowns and seven interceptions, while rushing for 349 yards and two touchdowns. The Ravens finished the season 8-9 and missed the playoffs, and they're hoping to avoid a repeat of the 2025 campaign.

away.headline: Ravens-Bengals: Four storylines beyond Lamar Jackson’s status
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens and Cincinnati Bengals have developed a rivalry with consequences that often extend well beyond one Sunday afternoon's score. Their recent battles have shaped the AFC North race, and with both teams coming off very different circumstances entering Week 7, another meeting will matter for the division's balance of power . Baltimore returns to M&T Bank Stadium after a disappointing 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns , while Cincinnati comes off its bye week looking to improve its position in a competitive division. The Bengals have enough talent to make this a tough afternoon for the home team, but beyond the immediate result, several storylines add weight to this matchup. From a familiar Baltimore advantage to the broader fight for AFC North supremacy, Sunday's game could add another meaningful chapter to this rivalry. Can Derrick Henry find some home magic against Cincinnati? The Ravens have enjoyed considerable success against Cincinnati at home, winning six of the past eight meetings overall and holding a 20-10 record against the Bengals in Baltimore. Derrick Henry has added another dimension to the matchup since arriving in Baltimore, bringing a powerful rushing presence that can change the way defenses approach the Ravens' offense. Henry has scored a rushing touchdown in three of his four games against Cincinnati since joining the Ravens. In the one game he didn't reach the end zone, he was exceptionally efficient, rushing for 100 yards on 11 carries for 9.1 yards per attempt. That performance illustrates how he can influence a game even without scoring. Baltimore needs its running game to become a source of stability after the offensive struggles in Cleveland. If Henry finds room early, the Ravens could build a more balanced attack and make life harder for Cincinnati's defense. His previous success against the Bengals gives the home crowd another reason to watch closely. Derrick Henry has another milestone within reach Henry's place in NFL history keeps growing, and Sunday's matchup could bring another significant moment. He needs 111 rushing yards to pass Jerome Bettis for eighth on the NFL's all-time rushing list, putting a milestone within reach if he finds the running lanes that have defined some of his best performances. Reaching that mark would add another accomplishment to Henry's remarkable career and give Baltimore another reason to keep feeding him the football. The Ravens cannot force the issue just to chase a personal milestone (and they won't), especially against a Cincinnati defense ready to challenge their ground game. However, if Henry gets into a rhythm, the pursuit of Bettis could become a compelling subplot to an important divisional matchup. Neither team wants to fall to 0-2 in the AFC North The AFC North remains tightly contested, making every divisional result especially important. home.headline: Lamar Jackson's Ankle Could Swing the AFC North Away From the Ravens Starting Sunday
home.blurb: Jackson was limited Wednesday and Thursday, his first practice work since spraining his left ankle Oct. 4 against Tennessee. If he can’t go, Huntley would make his third straight start . The defense has to hold up either way. Kyle Hamilton carries an 86.8 PFF grade , fourth among 98 qualified safeties, and leads all safeties with 18 stops. Trey Hendrickson, facing his former team, leads Baltimore with 20 pressures and has two sacks, and teammates have high expectations for him. Team sack leader Tavius Robinson (3.5) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday with a pectoral injury, which thins out a pass rush that stalled early. Baltimore has spent most of October reading injury reports before standings, and one national voice thinks that habit is justified. Bleacher Report’s Brad Gagnon picked the Cincinnati Bengals to win the AFC North and said Lamar Jackson’s availability and effectiveness after his ankle injury “could be major factors” in what has become a pivotal division game for the Ravens on Sunday. Pittsburgh, Cleveland and Baltimore all sit at 4-2, with Cincinnati at 3-2. Neither the Ravens nor the Bengals has a division win yet. Cincinnati is coming off its bye, and Gagnon noted the Bengals have the league’s easiest remaining schedule, according to ESPN’s Football Power Index . A road win would move Cincinnati toward control of the division. Ravens offense changes without Lamar Jackson Jackson has completed 68 of 96 passes for 967 yards, six touchdown passes and one interception, with a 119.6 passer rating and 144 rushing yards. With him on the field, Baltimore scored 116 points and 14 offensive touchdowns in 14 quarters, while the Ravens managed 40 points and four touchdowns in 10 quarters without him, ESPN’s Jamison Hensley reported . Tyler Huntley won in overtime at Atlanta, but the offense went quiet after the first quarter of a 13-10 loss in Cleveland that left Baltimore with questions . “Lamar wants to play. But at the same time, you have to be healthy enough to play,” Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters Wednesday . History explains why Jackson’s ankle carries so much weight. Since 2018, the Ravens are 11-2 against Cincinnati with Jackson and 0-3 without him, including the playoffs. A fourth loss in that column would hand the Bengals the head start Gagnon expects. home.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Eligible to Play vs. Ravens After NFL Reduces Discipline Upon Appeal
home.blurb: The Bills are on bye this week and will return to action on Nov. 1 in a marquee matchup with the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo has won back-to-back games after suffering its first loss of the season against the New England Patriots in Week 4. Bleacher Report • 5h Bears TE Out for Season Bleacher Report • 10h Jaylen Brown Calls Out Tatum 🧢 Buffalo Bills linebacker Sam Franklin Jr. will be eligible to play in Week 8 when the team returns from a bye after having his discipline reduced. Michael Signora, NFL senior vice president of football and international communications, announced on Friday that Franklin's appeal of his one-game suspension was reduced to a $14,926 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct by hearing officer James Thrash. The NFL announced on Wednesday that Franklin was being suspended for one game due to "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" during Buffalo's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. Franklin was said to have spit on a Raiders player during an extra-point attempt late in the fourth quarter. In a post on Instagram after the league announced its discipline, Franklin denied any wrongdoing: "Not a dirty player what so ever! Will always defend myself though. Still won't spit on anyone!" "As we said from the start, Sam did not and would never spit at an opponent, and there was no evidence that he did," Franklin's agents said in a statement . "We're glad the suspension was overturned and grateful to the hearing officer for a fair and thorough review. "It's unfortunate the league suspended Sam in the first place based on an unsupported accusation that received so much undeserved attention, and we hope the outcome is covered just as widely. We also hope the league takes a serious look at the opposing player's conduct, including striking Sam in the groin twice during the game. We're glad this is behind him, so Sam can get back to focusing on his teammates and next Sunday." Franklin was one of two Bills players disciplined for their actions during the Raiders game. C.J. Gardner-Johnson was suspended one game for spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. Officials flagged Gardner-Johnson for unsportsmanlike conduct and he was ejected from the game as a result of the incident. He issued an apology on social media following the Bills' win. Franklin is in his second season with the Bills after originally joining their practice squad in August 2025. He has appeared in 23 consecutive games since the start of last season. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. Going to venerated Wembley Stadium, facing off against the division-leading Jaguars, who had the advantage of having played in England the week prior and didn't have to worry about their body clocks, and managing to get away with a win was huge for the Texans. Houston, now at 2-4 but having won two straight road games against division rivals, returns to NRG Stadium to host the New York Giants of New Jersey. The Giants, sitting at 3-2-1, come into this matchup atop the NFC East, despite not winning in their last two games, a tie at Washington and a loss against New Orleans. In their last game, they fell to the Saints 34-27, but the Saints held a lead of 34-10 at one point in the 4th Quarter. They have only beaten the Giants once in 6 total meetings, and that was in 2002. Sandwiched between an international game and a bye week, this has the feel of a trap game for Houston. The team's updated Week 7 injury report lists him as a full participant Thursday, while Greg Newsome II remained a nonparticipant for a second consecutive day. New York hadn't published Friday game designations when this article was prepared. Any definitive statement about Sunday's cornerback lineup would get ahead of the available information. The Giants' depth chart lists Hood behind Newsome at one outside corner position. His availability becomes especially relevant while the veteran remains out of practice. Hood has appeared in five games with two starts, according to his NFL player record . Paulson Adebo is also practicing, but his status is different. The Giants designated him to return from injured reserve Wednesday, opening his practice window; he remained limited with a knee injury Thursday. Beginning that process isn't the same as being activated to the roster. Those distinctions prevent a misleadingly simple conclusion that the Giants have suddenly restored their cornerback depth. One player improved his practice participation, another remained sidelined, and a third is working through an IR return. None of those steps should be substituted for another. The opponent won't make an unsettled secondary's job easier. The Giants' weekly tracker noted that Houston coach DeMeco Ryans expects Tank Dell to return Sunday after his lengthy recovery from a serious knee injury. "If I get to go out there and play and start and do what I've gotten to do before, I'm excited," McFadden told Big Blue View earlier this week. McFadden was a full-time starter for the Giants in 2023 and 2024. In Game 1 last season, McFadden suffered a foot injury that kept him out for the remainder of the season. He admitted that "without a doubt" it isn't easy to no longer have a starting role. "Whenever you're used to something, you've had a taste of the pie, I guess, and then you don't get to go out there and eat with your boys anymore, it's tough, but I think it's just about staying present," McFadden said. "This game is a week-to-week basis, and obviously I had a pretty upsetting first week last year, and I learned a lot through that process, though. A lot of gratitude to be healthy and just to be able to play again, and I think that's what I found most throughout these past six weeks is just, just finding gratitude in whatever situation I'm in." The Giants designated cornerback Paulson Adebo to return this week, and it looks like he could be activated before Sunday's game. Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson goes runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals may be 2-4, but they're coming off a huge divisional victory over the Los Angeles Rams. The Cardinals are feeling it right now, and they're at home — but we know how Broncos Country travels, especially in the desert. At 4-2, the Broncos can't afford a slip-up — not if they want to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the division, and make their Week 8 rematch at Mile High a potential chance to get back to the top of the division, depending on what happens this Sunday with the Seattle Seahawks. That's me looking past the Cardinals a little bit. The Broncos won't be doing that. Sean Payton knows how to keep a team's focus on whichever game and opponent is up next, and that's the Cardinals. How will this one shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff see Sunday's action unfolding in Glendale, AZ. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 4-2 : Getting Bo Nix back in the flow of things has become like a quest for the Holy Grail. All the internal tinkering on Nix might not be as important as facing a Cardinals team the Broncos should beat. While most eyes will be focused on how Nix performs, it's returning rookie running back Jonah Coleman who steals the limelight with two scores. Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 4-2 : The Broncos' coaches and players are buzzing about a Nix breakout game. Looking at the Cardinals' 31st-ranked scoring defense — a unit allowing 350.5 yards per game — this is about as golden a get-right opportunity Nix could hope for. Courtland Sutton said , "At some point, the tide's going to turn" for Nix and this offense, and it happens at State Farm Stadium on Sunday. Nix passes for three touchdowns and 280 yards, while the Broncos romp in the desert. Pick : Broncos 27, Cardinals 17 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-2 : Only speaking for myself, the Broncos haven’t yet earned the benefit of the doubt. Not yet. But if there’s any way to earn that — and any day to have a get-right game — it’s Sunday against the Cardinals. This goes for the offense more so than the defense, which has been fantastic of late. If not now for Nix, then when? Go out there and dominate, and those “confidence issues” will miraculously disappear. I foresee a better showing, though maybe not quite the 2018 Kick Your A** blowout. This is an inferior opponent who, quite frankly, the Broncos should handily dispatch. “Should.” Pick : Broncos 30, Cardinals 16 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 4-2 : The Broncos' offense has been the source of much consternation. Is Nix hurt? Has the game passed Sean Payton by? Luckily, the Cardinals appear to be a get-right game. It's the NFL; there is no such thing as a guaranteed victory, but I expect the Broncos' defense and special teams, as well as continuity across the organization, to be felt in Arizona. I don't think the offense looks great... and even if it does, it's just one game, and the broader sample size should hold more weight in the total evaluation. Still, it will be nice to provide the fan base some hope. Pick : Broncos 20, Cardinals16 Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 4-2 : It's easy to think the Broncos will have their way with the Cardinals. But the Cardinals have shown they can challenge other teams , so it will be important for the Broncos' offense to come out strong. If the Broncos can do that and build a comfortable lead, the defense should be able to finish it from there, even with the Cardinals putting up a fight. Pick : Broncos 23, Cardinals 16 Trey McBride and Jacoby Brissett. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 3-3 : 10 days between games feels like forever, but reality is the Broncos have really hit their stride after their Thursday night game in each of the past two seasons. This won't be a dominant display, but it will be the first time this season both the Broncos' offense and defense play good complementary football, and Nix finds consistent success. Nix throws for a couple of touchdowns and rushes for another, giving fans some hope that he's close to being back. Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 3-3 : 10 days between games feels like forever, but reality is the Broncos have really hit their stride after their Thursday night game in each of the past two seasons. This won't be a dominant display, but it will be the first time this season both the Broncos' offense and defense play good complementary football, and Nix finds consistent success. Nix throws for a couple of touchdowns and rushes for another, giving fans some hope that he's close to being back. Pick : Broncos 24, Cardinals 13 Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 3-3 : If there was any opportunity to try to get the offense on track, it's this week against Arizona. Denver got the mini-bye, and Arizona's defense has allowed the most points in the league this season. Criticism of Nix is getting more intense by the minute, so it would be great to see him try to push the ball down the field and take chances against one of the worst defenses the league has to offer. I think he's gonna do it this week. Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 17 James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 2-4 : The Broncos are coming off a mini-bye, which frankly has come at a good time for a sputtering offense. Another week with Payton calling the plays again should be beneficial for Nix, but ultimately, the Broncos will have to play well to beat a tricky and plucky Cardinals team. The defense keys the win with a few takeaways off Jacoby Brissett, while the offense — just about — does enough to show some signs of life. Pick : Broncos 24, Cardinals 14 Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 2-4 : The Cardinals aren't pushovers and shouldn't be overlooked, but against their defense, the Broncos can get things jump-started. The Cardinals allow the second-highest explosive pass rate, which, despite ranking 18th in generating explosive offensive passing plays, is something the Broncos struggle with, as their 4.6% rate is 3% higher than Arizona's at 32nd. The Broncos' defense should be able to carry it enough to allow the offense to work things out, and this is the best opportunity for Nix and company to do that, similarly to the Dallas Cowboys game a season ago. The Broncos show progress in Arizona, and while they don't fix everything in a week, they do walk out with the win. Pick : Broncos 18, Cardinals 10 Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 2-4 : Nix and the Broncos have a chance to put up some major points against the Cardinals and their weak defense. The Cardinals have one of the worst defenses against the pass, teeing up Nix and the Broncos' receivers to breathe life into what has been a disappointing offensive start to the season. Defensively, if the Broncos can limit Trey McBride's impact, this should be their easiest win this season. Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner's exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the line of scrimmage on offense The Broncos offensive line has been the definition of "meh" to start the regular season. It's nowhere near what it's been the last few seasons, but it also isn't horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It's a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. Ya'll crazy if you think benching Bo Nix is even remotely the answer. That said, Bo Nix does need to play better, and he isn't seeing the field well to start the season. He's had slow starts in every season he's played, so, for now, I'm chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I'm hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos' schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. If the offense can up its game, this Broncos team will be unstoppable. — Sadaraine Limit the impact of Trey McBride The Broncos defense has performed well this season, aside from a few games. For the most part, they've been able to limit the impact of the opposing team's top player on their offense. This week, they face All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who is coming off a sensational 2025 season. He is the focal point of Arizona's aerial attack and gets over ten targets per game. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a good game plan that limits his impact on the game. away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. away.headline: Broncos Week 7 Injury Report: RB Tyler Badie Trending Toward Inactive
away.source: Denver Broncos On SI on MSN
away.blurb: Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday after missing the last four games. He still must be formally activated to the 53-man roster but is fully expected to play against the Cardinals. Coleman's return is especially helpful this week considering third-string RB Tyler Badie missed practice for a second straight day due to a thumb injury. His status for Sunday's game is in jeopardy; he needs a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up. Outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both also were DNPs this week. Hufanga will be ruled out on Friday, and the Broncos anticipate Elliss landing on short-term injured reserve, back at some point later this year. “He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," head coach Sean Payton said of Elliss on Wednesday. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) were limited participants; Surtain could be a game-time decision, though Waddle is expected to go. Arizona listed starting safety Budda Baker and running back Jeremiyah Love as DNP for a second consecutive day, as well as safety Andrew Wingard. Cornerback Garrett Williams and defensive lineman Darius Robinson were upgraded to limited. “They give you a couple different looks," Payton noted Wednesday. "They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback. I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.” Broncos Get Massive Boost with Return of RB Jonah Coleman Broncos' IR Watch: Who's Eligible to Return and What They Bring The Denver Broncos continued full-scale preparation for Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals, releasing their second injury report ahead of the Week 7 matchup. On it, running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) and cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) were listed as full practice participants for another day, while defensive end Zach Allen was upgraded to full after getting his usual rest day on Wednesday. Cardinals Might Be Down Some Starpower Unfortunately for the home team, the Cardinals are trending toward being at much less than full strength -- at least, according to their Thursday injury report . Baker's absence in particular would be a fortuitous break for a Broncos offense desperately seekin its first true breakout game in 2026. However, Payton knows well enough not to overlook the other 10 players on the Cardinals' defensive side. home.headline: Cardinals’ Jeremiyah Love gets official injury status for Broncos clash
home.blurb: Reports indicate that the 21-year-old ball carrier is officially ruled out against the Broncos, according to Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Love seemingly needs a little more time to recover from the injury before getting the green light to return. “Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) trying to get right after a high-ankle sprain, will miss another game this week. He’s been ruled out by coach Mike LaFleur,” Rapoport reported. With Love out for Week 7 against the Broncos, he’ll have his next chance to return from the injury in Week 8 against the Dallas Cowboys. Until he returns, Arizona will have to rely on the rest of the backfield for now. The Arizona Cardinals missed Jeremiyah Love in the 18-16 Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Rams, as the star running back is dealing with a high ankle sprain. With the club set to take on the Denver Broncos in Week 7, the franchise revealed Love’s status for Sunday’s matchup. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Tyler Allgeier will get the start on Sunday against the Broncos, while Zonovan Knight will likely get some opportunities too. Allgeier led the way with 18 carries against the Rams in Week 6, but Knight was much more efficient with his 15 attempts, leading the Cardinals with 80 rushing yards. This will be Jeremiyah Love’s second missed game this season. The Cardinals’ 2026 first-round pick has flashed potential early in his career, but it’s come with a lack of consistency. In his five appearances so far, Love has rushed for 245 yards and a touchdown on 67 attempts. He’s also recorded 11 receptions for 36 receiving yards and a score through the air. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Green Bay Packers in Week 7 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will take on a red-hot Green Bay Packers team that has won three straight games. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. picks.headline: Lions vs. Packers preview, prediction: On Paper
