LeBron's biggest comeback Lions vs. Packers preview, prediction: On Paper DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions plays against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jeremy Reisman Fri, October 23, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 12 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers are in town for a big NFC North matchup. The division is establishing themselves as one of the best in the NFL, so whoever wins this game will make an important statement, while the loser will have a bit of a hole to climb out of with three losses on the year. Which team has the statistical edge? Let's take a look in our On Paper Lions vs. Packers preview and prediction. Lions pass offense (13th in DVOA) vs. Packers pass defense (2nd) The Lions' passing attack continues to be one of the more reliable units on the team. Jared Goff has been amazingly consistent throughout his Lions career, producing a top-10 or top-five unit for four years running. Thus far this season, Detroit ranks: Second in passer rating (111.3) Seventh in yards per attempt (7.8) Third in dropback EPA (0.304) Fifth in dropback success rate (50.9%) Aiding Goff's MVP-like campaign is an offensive line that has come together quicker than expected. The Lions rank fourth in ESPN's pass block win rate (58%), third in PFF pass blocking grade (73.2), 11th in pressure rate allowed (32.4%), and 13th in sack percentage (5.4%). There has been some issues when it comes to blitzes (time to pressure is third-highest at 2.21), but that hasn't stopped Goff from being extremely efficient against the blitz (+0.33 EPA/pass, second-best). The only big question with this unit is how the return of starting center Cade Mays will impact the unit. Will he be an immediate upgrade from Juice Scruggs, who played well? Or will there be an acclimation period that will result in some missed assignments? The Packers are the most formidable foe the Lions have faced this year when it comes to defending the pass. Now, it's important to note that they have faced a few backup quarterbacks this year, including Carson Wentz, Jalon Daniels, Case Keenum, and Tyson Bagent. Still, last week's performance against the Cowboys was impressive, and shouldn't be pushed to the side. Thus far, Green Bay ranks: Third in passer rating allowed (73.9) Third in yards per attempt (5.9) Seventh in dropback EPA (-0.024) 14th in dropback success rate (45.5%) That last stat suggests a unit that may be bolstered a bit by big plays. And, indeed, that is at least part of the case. The Packers have successfully created a lot of sacks (15, 12th) and turnovers (nine interceptions, first). That is due to the aggressive nature of this defense. They make up for a mediocre defensive line with a high blitz rate (31.7%, 13th) and disguised coverages thanks to their elite pair of safeties. They rank second in total pressures (100), fourth in pressure rate (41.2%), and ninth in average time to pressure (2.58). They are able to do that despite ranking 30th in pass rush win rate (42%) and 26th in PFF's pass-rush grade (63.8). So if the Lions can manage the Packers' aggressive tendencies and avoid negative plays, this is a winnable matchup. Player to watch: Cade Mays. In his first game as a Lion, he may be one of the more critical pieces for the team. His presnap reads are going to be essential to Detroit's success, but that is something the Lions believe is one of his strengths. Via OC Drew Petzing: There's a stability factor there. He plays at a high level. He's big, he's physical, he's really smart. The communication piece is a huge part of playing that position. Advantage: Lions +1. This is a pretty dang even matchup, but the reason I'm giving the Lions an edge is because I believe Green Bay feeds off disruption, and Detroit has done a pretty good job avoiding that. Goff has yet to turn the ball over, and while I expect the Packers to get to the Lions quarterback for a few sacks, that shouldn't be enough to take them completely out of their rhythm. If the Packers are forced to blitz, Goff has proven he can beat that. Lions run offense (2nd) vs. Packers run defense (27th) It's been very feast or famine for the Lions' rushing attack, yet most of the statistics actually show this as a near-elite unit despite the inconsistencies. The Lions rank: 12th in yards per carry (4.4) Eighth in rush EPA (-0.033) Fifth in success rate (46.2%) Detroit is still seeking its first true explosive run, with Jahmyr Gibbs' longest rush of the season being just 22 yards, but it seems like it's just a matter of time given the underlying success of the unit. Run blocking is among the league's best, ranking first in PFF grade (78.1), fourth in adjusted line yards, and 20th in run-block win rate (72%). However, short-yardage situations have been a problem: the Lions rank just 20th in power success rate (62%) and they've been stuffed on 18% of rushes, which ranks 21st. Still, Gibbs has been impressive. His 18 rushes of 10+ yards ranks third in the NFL, despite playing one fewer game than most backs. Okay, so this is where things are going to look a little weird. On the surface, the Packers have been pretty darn good against the run. They've held half of their opponents below 90 rushing yards and four of six below 3.5 yards per carry. But they also got completely smashed by the Falcons, and some of their down-to-down consistency is not as good as the raw numbers look. Overall, the Packers rank: 15th in yards per carry allowed (4.0) 27th in rush EPA (-0.042) 25th in success rate (42.5%) How much is that being dragged down by the Falcons game? Not as much as you think. In the three games since playing Atlanta, Green Bay still ranks just 28th in rush EPA and 27th in success rate. If we include the Falcons game, over the last four weeks, the Packers rank 32nd in rush EPA and t-32nd in success rate. In other words, this is much more of a mismatch than it looks like. Player to watch: Javon Bullard. The Packers' nickel corner/safety is a force in the run game and will have to be accounted for on every play. Not only does he have a 85.3 PFF run defense grade, but he also has three tackles for loss. Advantage: Lions +2. I'm curious to see how involved the Packers' secondary will be in the run game because if they devote too many bodies to defend Gibbs, it could make them vulnerable on the back end. Still, I think this is a pretty clear advantage in Detroit's favor, but I'm capping the advantage at just two because the Lions have been inconsistent, and the Packers' "poor" run defense has really only cost them in one game. Packers pass offense (17th) vs. Lions pass defense (25th) It seems like the Packers' passing attack is in the midst of turning a corner—and that corner is finding an offensive line combination that isn't a complete disaster. Through the first couple of games, the Packers could barely field an offense due to injuries and subpar play along the offensive line. It's gotten a little better with some shuffling and additions, but the overall season numbers are still very concerning for Green Bay. They rank 25th in pressure rate, 32nd in time to pressure, 27th in pressures allowed, 32nd in pass-block win rate, and 32nd in PFF's pass-blocking grade. Yet, because they have very good weapons and a solid quarterback, their overall stats aren't as bad as you may think. The Packers rank: 15th in passer rating (91.8) 12th in yards per attempt (7.5) 14th in dropback EPA (0.131) 21st in dropback success rate (42.9%) Now, if you look at just the last three weeks, the Packers offense is clearly improving: Ninth in passer rating (101.8) Seventh in yards per attempt (8.2) Sixth in dropback EPA (0.248) 14th in dropback success rate (47.1%) As we've talked about all week, it's the Packers' deep ball that is most concerning this week, as Jordan Love airs it out more than any other quarterback in the league. The Lions' passing defense has been downright horrible, and you don't need me to show you the stats to prove it… but I'm going to anyways. Detroit ranks: 29th in passer rating allowed (106.3) 22nd in yards per attempt (7.5) 28th in dropback EPA (0.261) 30th in dropback success rate (52.7%) While big plays have been a huge problem (23 pass plays of 20+ yards allowed, third most), the high success rate allowed suggests there is no inflation with any of the other stats: they're just bad across the board. Even last game's "success" against the Cardinals looks more like playing a bad offense than playing good defense. But there is one saving grace, and it's the Lions' pass rush. Detroit sports PFF's third-highest pass-rush grade, ESPN's third-highest pass-rush win rate, and the fourth-highest sack rate in the NFL. Unfortunately, that only highlights how bad the coverage aspect of this team has been. Could the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch help? Absolutely. But I'm not ready to credit him as a huge difference-maker in his first game back from an Achilles. Player to watch: Matthew Golden. Of the Packers' 32 deep-ball attempts, 15 of them have targeted Golden. The second-year receiver has caught four of those for 173 yards (third-most deep ball yardage in NFL). That may not seem like a ton, but those are obviously four huge-impact plays, each gaining at least 36 yards. Advantage: Packers +3. Yeah, this is a pretty big advantage to give the Packers, but they're trending in the right direction, and the Lions are one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Yes, you could technically say the Lions are trending in the right direction after their performance against the Cardinals, but I am not convinced considering how poor Arizona's pass offense is. I expect a very strong day from Love. Packers run offense (32nd) vs. Lions run defense (23rd) I don't think there is any doubt in the world that the Packers' have the worst rushing attack in football. Their numbers are downright atrocious for the season. They've yet to hit 90 rushing yards in a game, nor have they rushed for over 3.5 a carry in a contest. For the year, they rank: 32nd in yards per carry (2.9) 32nd in rush EPA (-0.299) 31st in rush success rate (32.%) Unsurprisingly, the issues are mainly on the patchworked offensive line. They rank 31st in PFF's run-blocking grade (47.8), 32nd in adjusted line yards, but oddly 15th in ESPN's run block win rate. They rank 29th in rushing yards before contract per rush (0.74), and also 30th in rushing yards after contact per rush (2.26). That second number certainly has a chance to improve with Josh Jacobs expected back this week because Green Bay's running backs have also been poor (the Packers rank 32nd in rushing yards over expected per rush). But there is clearly a systemic issue here that Jacobs can't fix on his own. Last year, Jacobs actually ranked 33rd out of 35 running backs in EPA/rush, so he is not the savior Packers fans are hoping for. It's hard to get a grasp on the Lions' run defense. They've been awful in two games, awesome in two games, and neutral in one. It feels safe to call them average, and that's how the stats are looking, as well: 20th i

(Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Evan "Tex" Western Fri, October 23, 2026 at 8:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For a second straight week, the Green Bay Packers are playing in a game where the over/under on total points is set at 52.5. Last week, the team's matchup with the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field stayed well under the total, thanks in large part to an excellent effort by Jonathan Gannon's defense. This week, however, could be a very different story. On Sunday afternoon, the Packers play the Detroit Lions at Ford Field, a venue that has been the site of several high-scoring games between these two teams in recent years. FanDuel Sportsbook has the total points line set at 52.5 once again, the highest line for a game between these two teams since 2020, when it was set at a whopping 55.5. But since 2020, these two teams have generally scored early and often on the fast turf in Detroit: 2020: Packers win 31-24 (total: 55) 2021: Lions win 37-30 (total: 67) 2022: Lions win 15-9 (total: 24) 2023: Packers win 29-22 (total: 51) 2024: Lions win 34-31 (total: 65) 2025: Packers win 31-24 (total: 55) That's five of the last six games between these two teams in this venue going over 50 points, with four of them hitting 55 or more and two of them reaching a whopping 65 points. It's just what these teams do — well, except for in 2022, a game that was a bizarre defensive slugfest. But look at those results starting in 2023, when Jordan Love took over at quarterback — the Packers haven't scored fewer than 29 points at Ford Field with him behind center. Who will win the game? That's less certain, as the results above show, with the two teams each taking three of the last six games at Ford Field. APC is a bit split on this one, as you'll see in our picks below. But one thing we're not split on is taking the over. Given the Packers' issues defending against an elite running back earlier this year — and considering Jahmyr Gibbs is certainly in the Bijan Robinson echelon — plus the Lions' abysmal passing defense, this game should shape up to be a wild one. Here are our picks for Sunday's game, and give us your predictions in the comments!

picks.headline: Lions vs. Packers preview: 3 key matchups
picks.blurb: Lions vs. Packers preview: 3 key matchups - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 2 TRENDING World Series preview NFL injury updates Knicks change ring tune Cowboys not trading? LeBron's biggest comeback Lions vs. Packers preview: 3 key matchups Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard reacts to a play against Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Monday, Oct. 20, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Anthony Balaj Fri, October 23, 2026 at 10:30 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (3-2) will have an opportunity to reestablish themselves in the NFC North in both Week 7 and Week 8 as the Green Bay Packers (4-2) and the Minnesota Vikings (5-0) travel to Ford Field. This is not a situation most Lions fans are very familiar with. In my lifetime, the storyline with these types of divisional games was whether the Lions could finally establish themselves as true division contenders. But never to reestablish as one. Just take the 2025 NFC North standings in for a moment. Look at them again. I've seen the Lions at the bottom far too often in my 34 years. After getting the taste of what it was like at the top in 2023 and 2024, it felt like last place would never be the case again as long as Dan Campbell was leading the Lions. Unfortunately, it happened. Oh, and look. It could happen again because this division is the best in football. It's not slowing down. The race is on. Brian Flores and the Vikings defense is not waiting for the Lions young offensive line to gel before it comes to Detroit. Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears are not waiting for the Lions young defensive coordinator to find his footing while seeking to repeat as division champs. Matt LaFleur and the Packers are not waiting to the Lions secondary to solve its problems before attacking it with deep shot after deep shot. No, the Lions are at the bottom. Feel it. Breathe it in. Remember the decades at the bottom. In a way, it feels like this is truly the first game of the season. This is how it was always meant to be. Don't get me wrong, the 2023 and 2024 teams are without question the best and most memorable seasons of my Lions fandom. But the story of Dan Campbell's Detroit Lions was always meant to overcome adversity. To get kicked in the teeth. To get knocked down. But before long, they are going to be the last ones standing. Three key matchups. Three opportunity to reestablish . Ford Field vs. Packers' offense Green Bay comes into Ford Field ranking 29th in presnap penalties with 22 on the season . The key matchup here is the Lions fans at Ford Field against the Packers' discipline before the snap. Of course, presnap penalties are drive killer for most any NFL offense. But that is amplified for the Packers who have no running game and are last last in rushing yards per game (59.8), yards per carry (2.9), and rush EPA (-0.299) . Playing behind the sticks making the Packers even more one-dimensional would be extremely valuable for a Lions' secondary that could use all the help it could get, especially with rookie Keith Abney likely to play often at the safety position. In 2025, the Lions were the beneficiary on only 18 false start penalties, tied for 22nd in the NFL. To go with the 5-3 record on the season, Ford Field was hardly the home field advantage that it had been in the years prior. Sunday is an opportunity to reestablish Ford Field as being one of the most difficult environments for opposing teams to play in. Let me just drop this in here one more time. Kelvin Sheppard vs. poison picked The second key matchup was highlighted well by Jeremy Reisman's question to defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard asking how do does he decide on your poison in a matchup that presents both deep and over-the-middle weapons? "That is the coach's job to make sure that we understand the down and distancing, the tendencies and things like that. What have we seen? And obviously each game things change. You prepare. These coaches are good in this league and they self-scout as well." The Green Bay Packers' deep passing attack is a bit of a paper tiger with some interesting situational tendencies , but nevertheless, it must be respected out of the sheer frequency they attempt it. Last week against the Arizona Cardinals, Sheppard rolled out a unique solution by bracket covering both Trey McBride and Michael Wilson . It won't be that simple this week as the Packers have two deep threats in wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, as well as tight end Tucker Kraft. With the return of safety Brian Branch, Sheppard has the flexibility to pick his poison by game script, down-and-distance, and personnel groupings to put the defense in the best position for success. Branch's return to the field is an opportunity for the Lions secondary to reestablish itself, and it could not have come at a more critical time. Cade Mays vs. Jonathan Gannon Lastly, the third key matchup is Lions' center Cade Mays vs. Packers' defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon. Mays is set to make his Detroit Lions debut with his first start of the season. Gannon is in his first season as Green Bay's defensive coordinator and so far he has made some significant adjustments to his normal defensive philosophy. As discussed in "The Athletic Football Show" clip below, Gannon is dialing up blitzes of 6+ rushing defenders at 2-3 times the rate as he had in either Arizona or Philadelphia. It will be critical for Mays and Jared Goff to be on the same page regarding blitz recognition and communication. If successful, it is very likely the Lions offense reaches 30+ points scored against. Consider this Mays' introduction by fire to the blitz-heavy NFC North, wherein all three of the Vikings (1st, 66.7%), Bears (5th, 39.6%), and (Packers (10th, 32.1%) are in the top ten in the NFL in blitz rate, according to Sumer Sports . Mays has the opportunity to reestablish the Lions offensive line as one of the most intelligent and powerful units in the NFL since the retirement of Frank Ragnow. These are the matchups. These are the opportunities for the Lions to reestablish as the class of the NFC North once again.

away.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. Cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) does not have a game status and will play. ** Designated to Return from Injured Reserve - Currently within 21-day practice window * The Lions did not practice Wednesday; Practice participation designations for that day are based on estimations. news Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night news Packers list three questionable, two doubtful vs. Bears | Week 5 Injury Report DT Javon Hargrave (toe) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday news Packers rule out four, list two questionable vs. Buccaneers | Week 4 Injury Report OL Aaron Banks, Jacob Monk ruled out; LB Edgerrin Cooper questionable for Sunday Veteran linebacker won’t play Sunday after suffering injury at Thursday’s practice Wes Hodkiewicz packers.com senior writer Head Coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Friday morning that Franklin took a knee to his shin during a collision at practice Thursday. home.headline: Jordan Love, Christian Watson among Packers off injury report and set to play vs. Lions
home.blurb: Earlier this week, Packers quarterback Jordan Love told reporters he would be available to play on Sunday, despite being listed as limited on Wednesday with a back issue. Receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Savion Williams (ankle), and Matthew Golden (shoulder) are also off the injury report and are all set to play, despite being listed as limited all week. Guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), receiver Bo Melton (back), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackle Jordan Riley (Achilles) are all questionable. Head coach Matt LaFleur noted earlier on Friday that linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) is out after suffering an injury on Thursday . Love has no injury designation on Green Bay's final practice report of the week and is set to play against Detroit. Defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), and edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness) are also off the injury report and are set to play.

picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 2 TRENDING World Series preview NFL injury updates Knicks change ring tune Cowboys not trading? LeBron's biggest comeback Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. away.headline: Rams Week 7 Injury Report: More Bad News as Two Key Starters Face Uncertainty
away.source: Los Angeles Rams On SI on MSN
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are preparing to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, and the injuries just keep piling up. Earlier this week , the Rams placed wide receiver Davante Adams and nose tackle Poona Ford on injured reserve. Additionally, defensive lineman Kobie Turner has been ruled out for a handful of weeks. “Trent will be a DNP with his groin. We'll take it a day at a time, like what I told you guys, and evaluate his status as we go,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Then on Monday, found out Landman landed in the concussion protocol so he'll be a DNP.” While Landman's presence on the injury report isn’t surprising given that he’s been there the last few weeks, his placement in the concussion protocol is certainly a new development. In order to return to play, Landman will be limited in his allowed activity. He’ll then graduate to an aerobic exercise program overseen by the club’s medical staff. Lastly, after leaving Kobie Turner off the injured reserve transactions on Tuesday alongside Davante Adams and Poona Ford, the Rams placed him on injured reserve Wednesday. Turner will be out for a minimum of four weeks. In corresponding moves, the Rams signed EDGE Darryl Peterson III to the active roster and signed Jalen Hunt to the practice squad. “Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever and they're like, 'I have to trade a guy in and out now.' We're like, 'Well, that guy has worked his ass off for the last eight months to get this opportunity and it's unfortunate he doesn't get to do what he loves to do,’” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “I feel more for our guys than I do for anybody else.I know the work that they put into it to be out here doing what they love, so that hurts me for them. But at the same time, I think I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win.” For the Raiders, defensive lineman Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant as he remains in the concussion protocol. The Rams will certainly monitor the statuses of tight end Brock Bowers, offensive tackle Kolton Miller, and linebacker Quay Walker. All three were limited on Wednesday. However, the Rams will be monitoring other key starters as well this week. On Wednesday, cornerback Trent McDuffie didn’t practice with a groin injury and remains day-to-day. Additionally, linebacker Nate Landman has been placed in the concussion protocol. McDuffie was a late addition to the injury report last week. While McVay said that he felt good about him going into Sunday, McDuffie was inactive for the game. McDuffie will certainly be one to monitor this week. Once he passes that, he’ll be able to perform sport-specific activities.Step four involves returning to non-contact drills. That certainly raises concerns about his availability for the team's upcoming matchup. Fellow star receiver Davante Adams is already sidelined with a hamstring injury he suffered against the Arizona Cardinals. Head coach Sean McVay indicated that Adams will be out for six weeks. Defensive tackle Kobie Turner has a groin injury and is expected to miss a "handful of weeks." In addition, their new kicker Blake Grupe suffered a torn ACL in Week 6. There is some encouraging news regarding Garrett's return , as reports indicate he could return in Week 8 or shortly afterward, potentially giving the Rams' defense a major boost. away.headline: Report: Rams WR Puka Nacua's injury not believed to be serious
away.blurb: Per the report, his status is "up in the air" for the Rams (2-4) for Sunday's road game against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3). Los Angeles head coach Sean McVay is expected to speak to reporters on Friday. The Rams will be without fellow wideout Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a ruptured hamstring. The other members of the receiver room are Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman. Nacua, 25, has 37 catches for 417 yards and one touchdown to go with one rushing score in four games this season. He missed two games with a psoas injury. A two-time Pro Bowl selection, Nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions last season and racked up 1,715 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns in 16 games. Nacua left Thursday's practice early with the aforementioned calf injury. Head coach Sean McVay on Friday said Nacua "took part in a majority of the practice, left, (and then) got it checked out." McVay also said that "I don't think he (Nacua) knows exactly when it occurred." Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) is also listed as questionable. McDuffie did not practice all week. Meanwhile, inside linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) was ruled out, but is "making good progress," McVay said. With Landman out, McVay confirmed Los Angeles will elevate inside linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. home.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua questionable vs. Raiders due to calf injury
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams don't yet know whether Puka Nacua will suit up for them on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders . Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua will not practice on Friday and will officially be listed as questionable to play in Vegas. Nacua has already missed two games this season, sitting out Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip/groin injury. The Rams are already without Davante Adams, who ruptured his hamstring in Week 6 and will now miss 6-10 weeks. Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell could all see increased snaps with Adams out, and will become even bigger parts of the offense if Nacua misses Sunday's game. Nacua left Thursday's practice early after injuring his calf. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Friday that the injury is considered "more minor than anything else," and his status for Week 7 is "up in the air." This season, Nacua has 37 catches for 417 yards and a touchdown in the four games he's played. He also has three carries for 11 yards and a rushing touchdown. The Rams and Raiders kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET, which means inactives will be due 90 minutes ahead of time at 2:55 p.m. ET. At that point, we will officially know what his status is for the game.

This weekend, Seattle will host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City is coming off a frustrating 2025 campaign, which ended with a record of 6-11. That was the first time they had a losing season under Andy Reid, and they've already turned things around. Much of that is due to Kenneth Walker III, the former Seahawk who has been electric for the Chiefs . Seattle needs to find a way to contain Walker, while also figuring out how to get their ground game on track, which could happen with Zach Charbonnet set to return to action. Seattle is coming off a bad loss to Denver on Thursday Night Football in Week 6, as Sam Darnold threw multiple picks and the Seattle offense struggled to get anything going against an elite Denver defense. That dropped the Seahawks to 3-3, and they’re multiple games out of first place in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Kansas City defense put on a clinic in Week 6, holding the Los Angeles Chargers to just six points to move to 5-0 in the 2026 season. There is a huge revenge game possibly on Sunday, as Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since he won Super Bowl MVP for the ‘Hawks. The Seahawks let the star back go in free agency, and he’s been a monster for the Chiefs this season, rushing for 665 yards and six scores in just five games. Even though the Chiefs have a better record, Seattle is favored at home in this marquee matchup. Let’s take a look at the opening odds and some things to watch for in primetime in Week 7. That could be an issue for a Seattle team that is heavily reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, especially since Sam Darnold has thrown seven interceptions already this season. Seattle (No. 2 in EPA/Play on defense) completely shut down Bo Nix and the Broncos in Week 6, but it wasn’t enough with this offense still struggling. Seattle is just 25th in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate on that side of the ball through six games. It makes sense that the defending champs are favored at home, but there is one stat that I can’t look past when it comes to Mahomes. He’s been a road underdog 12 times in his career, going 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up. The Chiefs look like one of the best teams in the NFL, and I expect that to remain the case in Week 7. I don’t mind getting 2.5 points with them as an early lean for this primetime matchup. LeBron's biggest comeback NFL predictions: 4 game picks for pivotal Chiefs-Seahawks matchup John Tapia Fri, October 23, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Sunday Night Football brings the Kansas City Chiefs to Seattle for a Week 7 matchup, also unofficially known as the "Kenneth Walker III Bowl." If you're looking for player props and game-day value, check out the latest lines at FanDuel Sportsbook before kickoff. The Seattle Seahawks are coming off of two straight losses and are staring a sub .500 record straight in the eyes. The Chiefs meanwhile are undefeated and are currently elated with their recent running back signing (and Offensive Player of the Year candidate) Kenneth Walker III. Let's look at some game picks ahead of this matchup Sunday Night. Kenneth Walker III over 84.5 rushing yards (-114) I know Walker III is not a Seahawk anymore. However, considering his dominance this season, and the Seahawks lack of dominant running game, this is surely the game pick on the top of everyone's mind. Walker III is averaging 133 yards per game this season . Meanwhile the Seahawks defense has not allowed a 100 yard rusher in a franchise record, 35 games – not since October 27, 2024. One of these juggernauts will have to break in this matchup. The betting line being at 84.5 seems to be lower than many expected, or at least lower than I expected. Walker III is on a career heater right now. His ability to flip the field at any moment and break any run into a house call is very rare. Even if the Seahawks defense holds Walker III in check, it only takes one explosive run to get close to this 84.5 line. On top of this, Walker III already gets a large share of carries, and is now facing a revenge game. I would expect Walker III to get a ton of carries in this game, which means tons of opportunities to hit this line. All of this considered, it is tough to see Walker III not being able to hit at least 85 yards rushing. That doesn't mean that he will break 100 yards – the Seahawks could still very easily extend their streak to 36 games. However, this will be their hardest challenge yet. The pick: Kenneth Walker III over 84.5 rushing yards . Over 42.5 points (-112) The line for this game is 42.5, also a little lower. The Seahawks have scored at least 29 points four times this season. Their only two games where they scored less was in Week 1 with Drew Lock coming in with no first team reps, and in Week 6 with a short week Thursday Night Football game. Add to this, the fact that the Seahawks are playing the red hot Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs. There is a good chance that the Seahawks offense will need to keep up with Kansas City and their elite running game. That will surely be easier to do with Anthony Bradford and Zach Charbonnet likely returning for this game. Expect a high scoring affair in the battle of former AFC West foes. The pick: Over 42.5 total points (-112) . Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 92.5 receiving yards (-114). Leading the NFL in receptions (49), receiving yards (717), and receiving touchdowns (7) , JSN is once again on a heater. JSN has only missed the receiving yards line once this season – week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers where he put up only 76 yards (18.5 yards shy of the line). With the Seahawks run game struggling, and Sam Darnold looking less confident week in and week out, expect the safety blanket, JSN to have another big game this week against the Chiefs. Despite averaging 143.4 yards per game, the lines still remain fairly low. With it this low, the smartest move would be to bet the over. The pick: Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 92.5 receiving yards . Zach Charbonnet to score 2+ touchdowns (+750) The first three picks may not be too risky. However, this last pick is very risky. Trying to correctly guess who will score two or more touchdowns is a Hail Mary of sorts, but why not live on the edge? Charbonnet, who was just activated off of the PUP list , is expected to make his season debut against the Chiefs. This season, the Seahawks have struggled in short yardage situations. That is exactly where Charbonnet's return is huge. When on the field, Charbonnet tends to find the end zone. Last season, Charbonnet led the Seahawks with 12 touchdowns. The year prior, Charbonnet had 8 touchdowns . Although this will be his first game back since tearing his ACL in the 2025 playoffs, look to see Charbonnet get these opportunities once again. It isn't just the short yardage situations however. Charbonnet is also a strong pass catcher and gives the Seahawks an opportunity to score as a receiver as well. Despite only having one career receiving touchdown, Charbonnet still has 95 receptions for 693 yards in his young three year career. The other elephant in the room with Charbonnet's return is Kenneth Walker III's absence. Throughout his career Charbonnet has always split the backfield with Walker III. However, this season Charbonnet has an opportunity to prove he is the clear number one running back. With Jadarian Price still on injured reserve, and the other running backs on the roster proving lackluster, this week will be a perfect opportunity for Charbonnet to prove he can lead this backfield. The pick: Zach Charbonnet to score 2+ touchdowns .

away.headline: Travis Kelce Injury: 4 Chiefs Receiving Options Against Seattle
away.blurb: Kelce remained limited Thursday with an ankle issue. That does not mean he will miss the Seahawks game on Oct. 25, and it does not tell us how many snaps he could handle. It does mean Kansas City needs a plan that accounts for more than seeing his name on the active list. Noah Gray can absorb some tight-end receiving duties, Kenneth Walker offers underneath outlets, and Xavier Worthy supplies a downfield threat. The Chiefs’ Thursday injury report listed Kelce as limited for a second consecutive practice and wide receiver Rashee Rice as a nonparticipant. With Tyquan Thornton still sidelined following a dislocated ankle, Kansas City’s receiving options are thinning. A limited designation does not remove Kelce from the game plan, but practice participation doesn’t determine how Kelce will look when he plants, changes direction, or absorbs contact. Making up a backup plan in the middle of a stalled possession is the kind of stress that takes years off a Chiefs fan’s life. If Kelce is moving well, use him. If his ankle restricts him, my first adjustment would be to give Gray more receiving opportunities at tight end, with Walker available underneath and Worthy continuing to threaten downfield. Royals has supplied a useful scoring example, but I would need more evidence before expecting him to take on a major role. I would prefer an offensive plan with more detail than “Patrick and Travis will probably figure something out.” Travis Kelce Injury: 4 Chiefs Receiving Options Against Seattle Home The Travis Kelce injury has me paying more attention to the Chiefs’ receiving options than I’d like. Apparently, wondering how much his ankle can handle is now part of preparing for Sunday. away.headline: Fans fear for Josh Simmons' career as Chiefs star is ruled out again
away.blurb: He is currently dealing with a bulging disk in his lower back and will be out at least four more weeks - having already missed the first five games of the season. Last October, Simmons was involved in a bizarre and mysterious saga after he missed Kansas City's win over the Detroit Lions . Just hours before kickoff, he was listed as 'questionable' for 'personal' reasons before being downgraded to out. 'Josh worked his tail off. He worked diligently with my staff every day, and he improved to the point where he returned to practice in a limited capacity last week,' Burkholder said. MORE: Fury as winless Miami Dolphins announce they will hike ticket prices Josh Simmons' NFL future was plunged into more doubt on Thursday after the former first round pick was placed on injured reserve. Simmons was selected by Kansas City with the 32nd overall pick of the 2025 draft. It was hoped he would become their franchise left tackle. But the 23-year-old has started just eight games in a difficult start to his NFL career as injuries and personal matters have kept him off the field. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes later said he was surprised by Simmons' absence, with reports claiming coaches 'didn't know' where he was. Head coach Andy Reid was reluctant to discuss his absence but did say Simmons was 'taking care of family'. The left tackle later said he wanted to keep precise details 'in house.' He missed four games before eventually returning to the field in mid-November. Three games later, however, a fractured and dislocated hand landed him on IR for the remainder of the season. The 23-year-old showed up to training camp in late July hoping his injury issues were behind him. But on August 17, he reported feeling some discomfort in his calf, and the Chiefs' training staff determined it was stemming from his back. Chiefs trainer Rick Burkholder obtained an MRI exam that confirmed the herniated and bulging disk, which was 'higher up than we normally see in our offensive linemen, which complicated the case.' The Chiefs recommended a second opinion, and a back specialist in California believed that Simmons would be able to overcome the injury with rehabilitation rather than surgery. That is why the Chiefs had not put Simmons on injured reserve until Thursday. 'However we feel he plateaued in the recovery process... he's just not there yet.' After discussing the situation with Simmons, his family and representatives, the decision was made to place him on IR. 'It was decided and agreed upon by everybody,' Burkholder said, adding that surgery still is not in the forecast. It means undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will continue to protect the blind side of quarterback Mahomes, starting with Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.

away.blurb: The expectation, or maybe the hope, for Week 7 for the Seattle Seahawks was that running back Zach Charbonnet would be ready to play against the Kansas City Chiefs . Unfortunately, he won't play. He was ruled out again on Friday, according to head coach Mike Macdonald . Zach Charbonnet is out again for the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7 Also concerning is Nick Emmanwori being listed as questionable with a hip issue. Macdonald also said Drake Thomas and Chazz Surratt would be out, but that is expected. Neither practiced this week, and both missed Week 6. Surratt is a quality special teams contributor, but is replaceable. Thomas's starting inside linebacker spot will once again be taken by Tyrice Knight. The positive part is that right guard Anthony Bradford will return. His presence has been missed in the rushing attack. 12s should expect to see an uptick in performance from that part of the offense, even without Jadarian Price (still on IR) and Zach Charbonnet. Bradford can open a hole or two that backups Beau Stephens and Christian Haynes couldn't. The strange part was that Charbonnet seemed to be ramping up over the last few weeks. He was a full participant ahead of the Chiefs game and seemed destined to play. Even NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Charbonnet might get a heavy workload against KC . Kind of shows what the "insiders" really know. Charbonnet won't be playing against his former teammate, Kenneth Walker, who has been a star for KC this season. The kind of star that a healthy Charbonnet could have been for the Seahawks in 2026, but a knee injury in the playoffs last season forced him to miss time well into this season. Still, knowing that his absence ahead of Week 7, and with the Seahawks struggling to run the ball, is more disappointing than in previous weeks. Charbonnet's short-yardage excellence and red zone brilliance are what the team has missed. Many thought he would help the 3-3 team in Week 7. That isn't happening. The odd part is that Macdonald gave zero details on when Emmanwori's injury happened, other than saying it happened on Friday. He wouldn't even say if the injury happened during practice. The answer was frustrating. away.headline: He will get a hero’s welcome in Seattle — NFL analyst explains why Kenneth Walker III might avoid boos despite $43.05M move to Chiefs
away.blurb: Walker shared Seattle’s backfield with Zach Charbonnet for much of his time with the Seahawks, but Charbonnet was ruled out Friday and will not face his former teammate on Sunday. However, Walker was used as a bell cow down the stretch in the postseason and showed signs of what he is capable of if he were handed the lion’s share of the work. Only time will tell how the fans react to his return. It figures to be a key storyline during Week 7, and with the game on an island on Sunday Night Football, there figures to be plenty of discussion about it leading up to game time. Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle in Week 7 to face his former team for the first time since signing with the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency. The reigning Super Bowl MVP has been a force for Kansas City, while injuries and inconsistency have plagued the backfield that he vacated. It’s unclear how Seahawks fans will treat Walker in his first game back, but one NFL analyst believes he will be received back with open arms by the home fans. Mike Florio Believes Seahawks Fans Will Cheer Kenneth Walker When He Returns as an Opponent in Week 7 “I would assume that he will get a hero’s welcome in Seattle,” Mike Florio said of Kenneth Walker III. “A lot of times, when a guy leaves in free agency, (the fans) boo. There is no cause; he wanted to stay, folks.” He carried the ball 65 times for 313 yards and four touchdowns, while adding in nine receptions for 104 yards in three postseason games, en route to being named the Super Bowl MVP. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor After the dominant playoff run, Seattle let the talented running back walk in free agency, instead opting to allocate their money to extend Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Devon Witherspoon, Derick Hall, and Rashid Shaheed. Walker then signed a massive three-year, $43.05 million contract with the Chiefs in free agency, with $28.7 million guaranteed. Through five games with the Chiefs, Walker has been worth every penny, ranking as the No. 1 running back in PFN’s Running Back Impact Metric , registering 106 carries for 665 yards and six touchdowns, while adding 14 receptions for 95 yards and two touchdowns. “It’s hard because he’s still wearing the wrong uniform on Sunday night, but they have their first opportunity to truly appreciate him since the day of the parade,” Florio added. While fans may not like seeing him in another uniform, given the way things went down, they could still shower him with cheers in appreciation for helping deliver them a Lombardi Trophy. However, those cheers may quickly dissipate if Walker rips off a few big runs or scores on the home team. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker refuses to make his return to Seattle in Week 7 to face the Seahawks any bigger than it is
away.blurb: Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker refuses to make his return to Seattle in Week 7 to face the Seahawks any bigger than it is Skip to content Chiefs coaches have fielded questions all week about the return, and they don't expect it to get in the way of the task at hand. Their description of Walker was simple: Level-headed. His comments throughout the week reflect just that. Walker says he's treating this like any other week. Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy never returned to face a former team as a reigning world champion. He did face his former team as a player, though. The San Diego Chargers drafted Bieniemy in the 1991 NFL Draft, and he eventually played for the Cincinnati Bengals. Bieniemy didn't see the Chargers until Week 2 of the 1996 season. He had only two touches in that game: one carry for a 7-yard loss and a 9-yard reception. Regardless of the stat line, the experience gave Bieniemy insight into the emotions Walker could be feeling on Sunday night. Walker's RBs coach, DeMarco Murray, has also been through the same thing as a player. He faced the Dallas Cowboys as a divisional rival twice with the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2015 NFL season. Walker insists he won't make this matchup bigger than what it is. “It was mainly me and EB talking about how he went to a former team and how he felt about stuff, and you know, just giving me pointers on stuff like that,” Walker said. “But you just can't make it bigger than what it is. You know, I'm not the only one on this team. Everybody's going out there to play a game. I don't feel like it should be just about me.” That's the mentality of a true team player, and that outlook is part of what has made Walker's integration into Kansas City so seamless. He simply gets it. home.headline: Seahawks Questioned Walker’s Availability, Per This Report
home.blurb: Seahawks Questioned Walker’s Availability, Per This Report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 2 Seahawks Questioned Walker’s Availability, Per This Report Bob McCullough Fri, October 23, 2026 at 8:45 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs play the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night, and the Seahawks are faced with the prospect of stopping the running back who led them to the Super Bowl last year, then became the MVP of the final game of the season. Kenneth Walker III has been tearing up the league, and there's been talk that the running back could even step up to become league MVP based on the season he's having. So why didn't Seattle re-sign him? According to a report from Nate Taylor of ESPN, it was all about Walker's availability. It seems hard to believe based on what we've seen so far this season, but the writer said team officials had reservations dating back to his rookie season. They weren't entirely unfounded. Walker missed ten games during his first three seasons, which is why Seattle GM John Scheider spent a second-round draft pick on Zach Charbonnet, who split snaps with Walker last season. Walker's injuries included a hernia, separate ankle injuries, separate oblique injuries and a calf injury, and he also missed chunks of spring and summer 2025 with soreness in a foot and ankle. Taylor also reported that Seattle set a ceiling of around $10 million a year for re-signing Walker back in March. Meanwhile, the deal the Chiefs made with Walker that pays him an average of $14.25 million per season ranked fourth at the time among running backs, but it's since fallen to ninth. Seattle wanted to use Walker in what amounted to a timeshare, and the Chiefs were offering the running back something he badly wanted, which was a chance to be featured. According to Taylor, Walker totaled 3,251 scrimmage yards and 26 touchdowns while averaging roughly 17 touches per game during his first three seasons. During the 2025 regular season, that dropped to roughly 15 touches compared to 13 for Charbonnet, who averaged two more snaps per game than Walker -- 31 to 29. But Walker upped his game in 2025. He set career highs with 1,309 scrimmage yards and 4.6 yards per carry, and while he did score five touchdowns, Walker had to ceded opportuntiies in goal-line situations to Charbonnet, who got 12. The playoffs were a different matter entirely. When Charbonnet tore his ACL in the divisional round, Walker had 417 scrimmage yards and four touchdowns, averaging roughly 25 touches and 41 snaps, including a 161-yard performance against the New England Patriots in the Super Bowl in his first fully healthy season in the NFL. He committed to a clean diet and better sleep habits, and the Chiefs are reaping the rewards so far.

home.headline: Elijah Arroyo injury update: Seattle Seahawks receive devastating news as young tight end faces another major setback in promising NFL career
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Look, this injury hurts because Elijah Arroyo was just starting to carve out a role. The Seahawks took him in the second round of the 2025 NFL draft with the 50th overall pick. That’s real draft capital for a tight end. He tore his ACL in September of 2022 at Miami. That injury limited him to only nine games across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He bounced back and put together a great college career with the Hurricanes, which is a big reason Seattle used a second-round pick on him. Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo will miss the rest of the 2026 season, dealing another significant blow to his development after previous injury setbacks. How much more can Elijah Arroyo’s young career take? The Seattle Seahawks tight end is undergoing shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the 2026 season, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter . Arroyo got hurt in last Thursday night’s primetime loss to the Denver Broncos as he was trying to recover a fumble by wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. It’s a brutal way to lose a season, and it’s even tougher for a second-year player who still has a lot to prove. The numbers tell the story. Arroyo will miss 11 games for Seattle, plus any potential postseason run. Seahawks fans won’t see him on the field again until 2027. Arroyo’s development takes a hit As a rookie, he played in 13 games and caught 15 passes for 179 yards and one touchdown. Those aren’t eye-popping numbers, but they’re a reasonable foundation for a first-year tight end learning the NFL game. The 2026 season hasn’t gone the way anyone hoped, though. Through six games, Arroyo had just one catch for 17 yards, obviously much less production than his rookie year. Now he won’t get the chance to turn that around. This shoulder injury is going to set him back a good bit. A second-year jump matters for young tight ends, and Arroyo loses most of that year. Losing those reps hurts. Injury history follows Arroyo from Miami to Seattle Now, Arroyo’s injury history isn’t new . It just hasn’t involved his shoulder until now. Most of his problems have been with his knee. The knee issues followed him to the NFL, though. In December 2025, Arroyo suffered a Grade One knee strain. It resulted in the Seahawks placing him on injured reserve, and him missing the rest of the season. This shoulder injury is a different animal for Elijah Arroyo. It’s the longest absence of his pro career by a wide margin. For a player who has already lost chunks of time in college and the NFL, it’s another frustrating hurdle. What it means for the Seahawks’ tight end room I’m not going to pretend this changes everything for Seattle. It’s obvious Arroyo came in to be the No. 2 tight end, even as a fairly high draft pick. The Seahawks are set at the position with AJ Barner leading the way. Seattle’s passing game will keep running through its top options, and the tight end room isn’t suddenly in crisis mode. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Here’s a look at the odds, the latest movement since Sunday night and a quick preview of this primetime matchup. Cowboys vs. Eagles Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Cowboys -4.5 (-112) Eagles +4.5 (-108) Cowboys: -225 44.5 (Over -110/Under -110) Dallas opened as a 5.5-point favorite for Monday night’s showdown , but that line has quickly shifted towards the Eagles. Even with Jalen Hurts on injured reserve and out for the season, Philly has a shot to pull off an upset against a Dallas defense that is 31st in the NFL EPA/Play. Plus, the Cowboys’ offense looked awful on Sunday night in a loss to Green Bay, which may have caused the move in this line on Monday morning. Cowboys vs. Eagles Betting Preview The Eagles have covered the spread just once in the 2026 season (in their London loss to Jacksonville), so it’s hard to justify betting on them with a backup at quarterback. However, Dallas’ defense remains a bottom three unit in the league, and McKee (215 passing yards in Week 6) was at least able to move the Philly offense. If Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is able to return in Week 7, it could flip these odds even further towards the Eagles. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6. A win for Philly could bump it back up into at least the No. 3 spot in the odds to win the NFC East, but it seems pretty clear that oddsmakers expect Dallas to eventually figure things out and advance as the division winner. Bettors may want to consider the OVER (44.5) with how poor the Dallas defense has been this season. The OVER is 4-2 in Dallas’ six games and 3-3 in the Eagles’ matchup in 2026. away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Injury Report Heading Into Week 7
away.blurb: Let's take a look at some of the injuries the Dallas Cowboys have dealt with throughout the 2026 NFL season, looking at both sides of the ball and who is out short and long-term. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown has been sidelined since suffering a hamstring injury in Dallas' Week 1 game against the New York Giants. He was initially expected to miss just one or two games but has now missed five consecutive games. Luckily for the Cowboys, Overshown has been medically cleared and is expected to return against Philadelphia this week. Cornerback Cobie Durant has also missed significant time after suffering a hamstring injury against the Washington Commanders in Week 2. Durant hasn't played since that game but is nearing a return. Dallas' secondary has been shredded all season, so the Cowboys will be hoping Durant returns soon alongside the recently acquired Joey Porter Jr. Overshown was a full participant in Thursday's practice , marking his first full team practice since suffering his hamstring injury. Meanwhile, Durant returned to practice as a limited participant and is trending toward playing Monday. Wide receiver and return specialist KaVontae Turpin suffered a rib cartilage injury against the Packers and did not participate in Thursday's practice. Linebacker Dee Winters , who recorded an interception in Dallas' Week 6 game against the Packers, also suffered an Achilles strain against Green Bay and did not practice Thursday. Winters is currently listed as doubtful and is expected to miss the Cowboys' Week 7 game against the Eagles.
