away.headline: All because of his contract — Cowboys legend Dez Bryant defends George Pickens amid Dallas’ questionable treatment of star WR
away.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys are 2-4 after a 23-13 loss at Green Bay. This week, the attention has turned to George Pickens, the star receiver playing out the 2026 season on the franchise tag, with head coach Brian Schottenheimer telling reporters Thursday that Pickens “needs to understand that he impacts us in the running game as well.” Cowboys legend Dez Bryant, however, defended the receiver on Friday, writing that “Pickens is still human. He has emotions.” The former Dallas wideout went further in the same post, tying how the Cowboys use Pickens to the contract he is playing under. Dez Bryant Points to George Pickens’ Contract Bryant didn’t hold back on the Cowboys’ approach. He wrote that they “only go to him in notable, critical situations and rely on him to make a play,” and that it was “all because of his contract.” Bryant then added: “The psychology behind it is what’s messed up, and it doesn’t work in his favor when the world thinks he doesn’t care… let’s really talk about it.” Schottenheimer, speaking a day before Bryant’s post, gave a different read on Pickens’ emotions: “GP is one of those guys where I don’t ever see him really affected in terms of, you know, the emotion.” He also took up the question of touches. “Does he get the ball? Does he not get the ball? If these guys play a lot of snaps, I think part of it is us rotating those guys through.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor The rest of his message was about the running game, with running back Javonte Williams as the model: “You know, he’s got to do the same thing in the run game — picking up safeties and blocking corners — just like Javonte does, picking up blitzes so he can catch balls. That’s part of the team-first mindset, and GP does understand that.” Dallas ran the ball 15 times for 48 yards against the Packers. Pickens has faced questions about his effort before. During his time with the Pittsburgh Steelers, before his move to Dallas ahead of the 2025 season, he drew criticism for taking plays off when the ball wasn’t coming his way and for his run blocking. The contract Bryant mentions is the $27.3 million franchise tender Pickens signed for 2026. “Like the tag and all that, it’s just football first. So, definitely play football first, kind of like I did last year … let my agent worry about it, really,” Pickens said at mandatory minicamp in June. The July 15 deadline for a long-term deal later passed without one. What the Numbers Say About Pickens’ Role Pickens has caught 33 of his 52 targets for 428 yards and one touchdown this season. His catches are tied for 11th in the NFL, and his yards rank 12th, and Pro Football Network’s NFL WR Impact Grade has him at 79 this season, 19th of 82 graded wide receivers. home.headline: Eagles linked to Steelers QB after brutal Jalen Hurts injury news
home.blurb: Seeing the Eagles be viewed as a team that could target Rudolph is understandable. With Hurts being out long-term, the Eagles would benefit by adding another quarterback with NFL experience to their depth. While Rudolph is not a star like Hurts, he would give Philadelphia another QB option to work with as they aim to get their season back on track. Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. “Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He’s one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar,” Knox wrote. “Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles.” Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline. home.blurb: NFL Fans Demand 'Investigation' Into Philadelphia Eagles' Medical Staff - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 2 Andrew Holleran Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:49 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Eagles are likely to be without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season, as he's being put on blood thinners, the team announced on Monday. Hurts missed this past Sunday's game after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot. He had previously played in a loss to the Jaguars in London earlier this month. "Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. 'blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football," the team announced. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery." Hurts last played in a loss to the Jaguars in London. He threw for 220 yards and one touchdown in a 19-17 loss. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reports that Hurts stayed up for about 36 hours straight before that game, after being diagnosed. "How committed is Jalen Hurts to football? After initially being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London, doctors told him not to sleep as a precaution, so he had been awake for roughly 36 hours when he started against the Jaguars, throwing for 220 yards and a TD," he reported. home.headline: Philadelphia Eagles sign ex-New York Giants OL Evan Neal
home.blurb: The Alabama product was taken seventh overall by the Giants in 2022 and went on to appear in 29 games with 27 starts, all of them at right tackle. Injuries and recurring struggles in pass protection limited his production over those seasons. Head coach John Harbaugh gave Neal a clean slate this offseason on a one-year deal, only for the team to release him during final roster cuts in August. After a brief stop on the Las Vegas Raiders’ practice squad, Neal worked out for the Eagles on Wednesday, practiced with the team Thursday, and was officially added as a guard. Former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal has landed with the Philadelphia Eagles , who signed the 2022 first-round pick to their practice squad on Thursday. New York moved Neal inside to guard ahead of 2025, but he never took an offensive snap and spent time on injured reserve (IR). The move provides Philadelphia additional depth amid ongoing offensive-line concerns. From the Giants’ perspective, Neal’s arrival in Philadelphia closes another chapter on a high draft investment that never developed into the long-term starter the franchise once expected. New York has continued to reshape its offensive line without him as he searches for a foothold elsewhere.
